issues.title: Duplicate CAXACAXACAXA delimiter appended to Windows stub corrupts self-extracting executable
issues.test: none added (claim does not hold); checked by reading the bytes of the packaged Nextra.exe 2.1.6 and by running rcedit on a copy of caxa's Windows stub
issues.proof: The claim's premise is wrong: the caxa 3.0.1 packager never writes the separator. For a stub it copies the stub, appends the gzip tarball and a JSON footer (node_modules/caxa/build/index.mjs lines 104-107); the separator ships at the end of the stub file itself (package.json prepare:stubs), as a 14-byte overlay after the PE image. rcedit rebuilds the PE with a .rsrc section and drops that overlay: on a copy of stub--win32--x64, separators went 1 -> 0 after rcedit (3495438 -> 3540480 bytes) and 0 -> 1 after the appendFileSync at scripts/package-app.js:377. The packaged Nextra.exe 2.1.6 (built Oct 24 from the current script, smoke test passed) holds exactly one separator, at offset 3540480 = the end of its PE image, followed by 1f8b08 (gzip header); no back-to-back separators. The stub reads the archive after the first separator (stub.go line 102, bytes.Index), so that layout is correct. Without line 377 the exe would have no separator and the stub would stop with 'Failed to find archive'.

issues.title: isLocalHostname fails open on missing or unresolvable hostname values
issues.test: none added (claim does not hold); checked with a scratch script that loads lib/network.js and lib/requestIdentity.js and runs copies of server.js isPublicOrigin (lines 236-249) and getShareBaseUrlFromHeaders (lines 580-596) for a remote client with no, empty and odd Host values
issues.proof: The literal behaviour is as reported (isLocalHostname(undefined|''|'unknown') = true, lib/network.js:35), but it fails closed. isLocalHostname makes no access decision: its only callers are server.js:248 isPublicOrigin, :466/:474 getShareBaseUrl and :585/:592 getShareBaseUrlFromHeaders, and each uses !isLocalHostname(...) to decide whether a host may become a public share URL, so 'local' means nothing is advertised. The empty case never reaches it: isPublicOrigin guards with !!hostname, and parseUrlHostParts (lib/requestIdentity.js:9-23) returns null for undefined, '', '   ' and ':3000', so the hostParts && guard skips the call. Script output for remote peer 203.0.113.9: no Host -> shareBaseUrl '', empty Host -> '', Host 'unknown' -> '' (with 'unknown' treated as non-local it would become 'http://unknown', i.e. the change the claim implies would reflect more client input, not less); operator classification 'remote' in every case. Operator and relay trust come from classifyClient/isLoopbackIp/isLocalClientIp on the peer IP (server.js:306-339), and isLocalClientIp returns false for 'unknown' (lib/network.js:14). lint, typecheck and npm test (421/421) pass on the unchanged code.

issues.title: Synchronous URL revocation in downloadDiagnosticBundle aborts file downloads
issues.test: none added (claim does not hold); checked with a scratch Playwright script that loads the unchanged src/lib/diagnosticBundle.mjs into a routed page (no network) and calls downloadDiagnosticBundle in Chromium 153 (headless shell and full build), Firefox 155 and WebKit 26.6, reading back every downloaded file, plus a control that revokes the URL before the click
issues.proof: The revoke cannot reach a download that has already started: click() runs the anchor's activation behaviour synchronously, and the HTML 'download the hyperlink' steps parse the href before going in parallel; the URL parser resolves a blob: URL's blob URL entry at parse time and the blob fetch reads that entry, so revokeObjectURL (src/lib/diagnosticBundle.mjs:206, after link.click() at :203) only removes the store entry for later parses. Script output: in all four engine builds 15/15 downloads completed with exactly the bundle JSON (2,000, 5,000,000 and 50,000,000-char bundles x 5 each, revoked in the same tick as the click), download.failure() null each time. The control, which revokes before the click, does fail (Chromium: download failed 'canceled'; Firefox and WebKit: no download started), so the check sees a revoked blob when there is one. lint, typecheck and npm test (421/421) pass on the unchanged code.

issues.title: Missing host authorization in connect-transport allows viewers to hijack or break host send transport
issues.test: tests/socketConnectTransport.test.js: 'only the host can connect the host send transport'
issues.proof: Holds. lib/socket.js connect-transport looked the room up with findRoomBySocket (lib/rooms.js:203-207, which matches viewers as well as the host) and then connected room.hostTransport whenever the transportId matched, with no room.hostSocketId === socket.id check, unlike create-send-transport and produce, which use findRoomByHost. The new test (real socket.io server, stub transports) has a joined viewer send connect-transport with the host's send-transport id; on the unchanged code it failed at line 71: 'Expected values to be strictly equal: true !== false' (the viewer got success: true and the host transport's connect() ran with the viewer's DTLS parameters). Since mediasoup throws 'connect() already called' on a second connect (worker/src/RTC/WebRtcTransport.cpp:521), a viewer that got there first would also break the host's own connect. The reported severity is overstated: transport ids are crypto.randomUUID() (mediasoup node/lib/utils.js:29-30) and the server sends the host transport id only in the host's create-send-transport reply, so a viewer cannot guess it; the gap matters only if the id leaks. Fix: the host-transport branch now also requires room.hostSocketId === socket.id; a viewer falls through to its own recv transport and otherwise gets 'Transport not found.'. After the fix the test passes, including the host connecting its own send transport and the viewer its recv transport.

issues.title: fMP4 parser discards ftyp on stream restart producing incomplete init segment
issues.test: none added (claim does not hold); checked with a scratch script that drives a real FFmpegRelay (lib/ffmpegRelay.js) with the real FFmpeg 2025-10-21 build and a 120-frame H.264 stream, through an unexpected exit (stdin EOF, code 0, so the exit handler calls restart()) and a reconfigure(5000), logging the parser state in which every ftyp and moov box arrives and the boxes of every init segment the relay emits
issues.proof: The parser does what the claim describes in isolation (lib/fmp4Parser.js:152-198: in 'streaming' state ftyp is ignored and a later moov becomes the init on its own, line 195), but the claimed trigger never reaches that state. Each FFmpeg process writes exactly one ftyp+moov, at its start (empty_moov; the mov muxer never writes another), and FFmpegRelay resets the parser to 'init' before every spawn (start(), lib/ffmpegRelay.js:331) and in stop() (:530), which restart() (:576) and reconfigure() (:554) call before starting the new process. Script output: ftyp and moov arrived in parser state 'init' for process 1, process 2 (after the unexpected exit and restart(), restartCount 1) and process 3 (after reconfigure()); the relay emitted three init segments, each ftyp+moov (794 bytes), and 135 fragments; raw stdout of each process held one ftyp and one moov. Counterfactual: feeding process 1's and process 2's captured output into one parser with no reset gives inits 'ftyp+moov | moov', so the moov-only init appears only if the reset is removed. The other caller, the browser MP4 recorder relay, builds a new parser per recorder generation (lib/socket.js:2727-2739, lib/relayMp4.js:202), drops chunks of any other generation (lib/socket.js:2643), and each new MediaRecorder takes a new generation (src/HostView.jsx:800, :809). lint and typecheck pass; npm test 422/422 on a rerun (the first run had one failure in tests/churnRuntime.test.js, 'Internal error' on every churn operation, which passed alone and in the full rerun; code unchanged).

issues.title: normalizeCloudflareIceServersPayload ignores object-shaped iceServers responses
issues.test: none added (claim does not hold); checked with a scratch script that loads the unchanged lib/cloudflareTurn.js and runs fetchCloudflareTurnCredentials against a stubbed fetch (no network) returning Cloudflare's documented generate-ice-servers response, plus extractCloudflareTurnConfig on the object-shaped payload the claim describes
issues.proof: The literal behaviour is as reported (lib/cloudflareTurn.js:35-39 returns [] unless iceServers is an array, so an object-shaped payload throws 'Cloudflare did not return any browser-safe TURN URLs.'), but that payload never reaches it. The only caller, fetchCloudflareTurnCredentials (server.js:732 via loadCloudflareTurnCredentials, for POST /api/cloudflare-turn-credentials), always calls POST /v1/turn/keys/{id}/credentials/generate-ice-servers (lib/cloudflareTurn.js:113-115, unchanged since the module was added in a5ae600). Cloudflare documents that endpoint's 201 response with iceServers as an array: one STUN entry, one TURN entry with urls, username and credential (developers.cloudflare.com/realtime/turn/generate-credentials/). The single-object shape { iceServers: { urls, username, credential } } is the response of the other endpoint, /credentials/generate, which this code does not call. Script output: request to https://rtc.live.cloudflare.com/v1/turn/keys/key-id/credentials/generate-ice-servers with body {"ttl":86400}; the documented array response gave turnConfig with 5 browser-safe TURN URLs (port 53 dropped), authType static, username and credential set; the object-shaped payload threw the error above. The existing test 'Cloudflare TURN parser extracts static credentials and browser-safe TURN URLs' (tests/cloudflareTurn.test.js:28) already uses the documented array shape. If Cloudflare ever changed the shape, the operator would get a 502 with that error message (server.js:821-825), not a silent failure. lint and typecheck pass; npm test 422/422 on the unchanged code.

issues.title: OBS profile write and encoder listing are gated only by a 'loopback' check, which local cloudflared tunnels may satisfy
issues.test: none added (claim no longer holds on dev); checked with a scratch probe that spawns the real server.js on plain HTTP with a quick-tunnel SHARE_BASE_URL and a temp APPDATA holding a fake OBS profile and log, connects Socket.IO clients with the headers cloudflared forwards, creates an OBS room and calls obs-encoders and obs-encoder-settings; run once on dev and once on a git-archive snapshot of 5b40efb (the code before TASK-053)
issues.proof: Held at audit time, removed by TASK-053 (40a7e0a). The gate is as described: server.js:1572-1578 lets applyObsEncoderSettings and listObsEncoders through only when getSocketClientClassification(socket).kind is 'loopback', and lib/socket.js:2020-2059 additionally requires the socket to host an OBS room. The quick tunnel's origin is 127.0.0.1 (lib/tunnel.js:191), so its sockets do come from a loopback peer. On dev, getSocketClientClassification (server.js:291-298) passes viaKnownProxy = isKnownPublicShareRequest(headers) || isRelayedFromLoopback(headers, peer), and classifyClient returns 'known-proxy' before it ever checks loopback (lib/network.js:88-91). isRelayedFromLoopback (lib/requestIdentity.js:79-82) is true for a loopback peer carrying any Cloudflare header (cf-connecting-ip, cf-ray, or cdn-loop containing 'cloudflare'; lines 39-44), and isKnownPublicShareHost (64-70) matches the share Host without its scheme. Cloudflare sends CF-Ray to every origin and neither the visitor nor a zone's transform rules can remove cf- headers other than cf-connecting-ip (developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/reference/http-headers/, /rules/transform/request-header-modification/), so every tunneled socket carries relay evidence. Probe on dev: the control (local socket, Origin http://127.0.0.1:port) created an OBS room without a token, got encoders ['jim_nvenc','obs_x264'] and applied:true, file written; every relayed variant (share Host + Cloudflare headers with a share Origin or a forged local Origin; local Host and Origin with Cloudflare headers, cf-ray only, cdn-loop only, or cf-connecting-ip only; share Host only) needed the operator token to create the room and then got encoders null, applied:false, reason 'not-local', no file written. Same probe on 5b40efb: every relayed variant except the share-Origin one created the OBS room without a token, listed the encoders and wrote streamEncoder.json (applied:true), because the old code built the Host origin with the listener's scheme (http) and ignored Cloudflare headers. lint and typecheck pass; npm test 422/422 on the unchanged code.

issues.title: Stale or closed WHIP WebRtcTransport DTLS handler corrupts room state and triggers premature session teardown
issues.test: none added (claim does not hold); scratch probe .arbitra/dev-notes/results/check-08-probe.cjs (real mediasoup 3.27.1 worker, router and UDP WebRtcTransports on 127.0.0.1, the real WHIP router on a real HTTP server; DTLS state changes delivered through mediasoup's own Channel.processNotification, as the worker delivers them), run on dev c7489d0 (lane lifecycle) and with ac1c688's lib/whipRoutes.js, whip.js, rooms.js, roomMediaPipeline.js, sessionRegistry.js and roomLifecycle.js written over the lane and restored afterwards; outputs check-08-probe-output-dev-c7489d0.json and check-08-probe-output-ac1c688.json
issues.proof: Does not hold, now or on ac1c688 (the dtlsstatechange listener is unchanged: lib/whipRoutes.js:421-535 now, :410-524 at ac1c688). What is true: the 'failed'/'closed' branch (:516 now, :505 then) has no generation or transport check, unlike the 'connected' branch (:424). What is false: that a transport the server closes runs it. mediasoup 3.27.1 Transport.close() removes the transport's channel subscription synchronously before asking the worker to close it (node_modules/mediasoup/node/lib/Transport.js:147; routerClosed :188 and listenServerClosed :224 do the same), and WebRtcTransport.close() sets dtlsState to 'closed' without emitting (WebRtcTransport.js:117-128). dtlsstatechange is emitted only from the worker-notification handler (WebRtcTransport.js:220-230), which Channel dispatches by handler id in a setImmediate (Channel.js:304-311), so a notification still queued at close time finds no listener. Every path that drops room.whipTransport closes it: closeWhipSession (:117-122, run by the replacing POST :335 and by DELETE :616), cancelPendingStart (:269-271), the superseded check (:396-399), the POST catch (:573-576), the no-fingerprint 400 (:412) and the roomLifecycle fallback (lib/roomLifecycle.js:25-31). So no open transport other than the room's current one ever has this listener, and for the current one the grace path is the intended behaviour. Probe, identical on both revisions: (A) a closed WebRtcTransport has 0 channel listeners (1 before), dtlsState 'closed', events only observer:close; (B) control: a DTLS 'closed' delivered to the current transport reaches the handler (whipReconnecting true, grace timer set, 1 host-metrics call, session closed after the 150 ms grace), so the probe sees the branch when it runs; (C) after a replacing POST, 'closed' and 'failed' delivered to the replaced transport reach nothing: no events, no grace timer, whipReconnecting false, 0 host-metrics calls, and the new session and its open transport are still current after the grace period; (D) the same after DELETE (session stays closed, not revived into reconnecting); (E) a 'closed' notification already queued when closeWhipSession runs reaches nothing; (F) a client abort while transport.connect() is pending, with the listener already attached, leaves no grace timer or reconnecting state. (G) only under the claim's premise, with close() patched to emit dtlsstatechange 'closed' first, does the replacement session get a grace timer and get closed at expiry; mediasoup does not do that. No code changed. Checks on the unchanged lane: node --test tests/whipRoutes.test.js 7/7; npm run lint and npm run typecheck pass; npm test 1080/1080.

issues.title: Coverage gate calculates directory depth incorrectly causing double slashes and universal target misses
issues.test: `node scripts/coverage-gate.js` (the gate itself, on Node 22.14.0), plus a scratch harness that preloads a spawnSync stub (`node -r scripts-check-09-stub.js scripts/coverage-gate.js`) so the unchanged gate parses canned reports: the real Node 22.14 report, the same report with 2 spaces per level as the claim describes, a flat report with backslash paths, and the real report with lifecycleController.mjs lines lowered to 50%
issues.proof: The claim does not hold. Node's coverage report indents one space per tree level, not two: the reporter source embedded in node.exe 22.14.0 builds each row as `${prefix}${StringPrototypeRepeat(' ', depth)}${getCell(file, filePadLength - depth, ...)}` and recurses with depth + 1, and the real report reads '# lib', '#  roomMediaPipeline.js', '# src', '#  lib', '#   lifecycleController.mjs'. So rawName's leading-space count is 0, 1, 2, pathAtDepth stays dense, and the joined paths are 'lib/roomMediaPipeline.js' and 'src/lib/lifecycleController.mjs', which are in targets. `node scripts/coverage-gate.js` exits 0 with 'Coverage thresholds passed for 4 runtime files.' (52 tests pass). The harness shows the gate is not passing vacuously: lowering lifecycleController.mjs lines to 50% gives 'src/lib/lifecycleController.mjs: lines 50% is below 70%' and exit 1, and the flat backslash layout also passes. Only the claim's hypothetical 2-space report reproduces the described misses ('no coverage result' for all four targets, exit 1), i.e. the gate would fail closed, never pass silently. Not real on the original code either: `git diff ac1c688 HEAD -- scripts/coverage-gate.js` is empty, and the report format comes from Node (package.json engines >=22.0.0; 22.14.0 is the only Node on this machine). No file changed.

issues.title: Single-encoding video streams are severely throttled by index-based simulcast mapping
issues.test: A browser probe (results/check-10-probe.cjs; output in check-10-probe-output.json). It runs the real app, built with vite into the scratchpad, against the real server.js (NEXTRA_SMOKE_TEST=1, ports from claimServerPorts) in Playwright Chromium 153 and Firefox 155. The Playwright lock was held. It hooks RTCPeerConnection.prototype.addTransceiver, starts sharing a stubbed 1280x720 capture, switches the live profile 1440p/60 -> 1080p/30 -> 4K/60, and reads the producer sender's getParameters().encodings after each step. A second check (results/check-10-unit.cjs) slices the unchanged getSimulcastEncodings and applyProducerBitrateProfile out of src/HostView.jsx, at HEAD and at ac1c688, and runs them against fake senders with 3 encodings and with 1.
issues.proof: The claim does not hold. Its premise, a video sender with only one encoding, never happens in Nextra. The only video produce() call (src/HostView.jsx:1500-1504) always passes getSimulcastEncodings(), i.e. [r0, r1, r2]. The mediasoup-client 3.24.5 handlers (Chrome111.js:240-265, Firefox120.js:254-268, Safari12.js:241-266) give each one rid r${idx} and pass them in that order to addTransceiver's sendEncodings, without reordering. mediasoup-client's own setMaxSpatialLayer (Chrome111.js:459-468) maps encodings by index on the same assumption. In the probe, both browsers kept 3 encodings in order rid r0, r1, r2, and after every profile change each one held its own rid's target. For example, at 1440p/60: [0] r0 2520000, [1] r1 8400000, [2] r2 21000000. At 4K/60: 4320000, 14400000, 36000000. So nothing was capped at the r0 share. Even in the hypothetical case: a browser that cannot simulcast trims sendEncodings from the tail (webrtc-pc addTransceiver, maxN), and an answer that rejects simulcast keeps the first encoding. Either way the lone encoding left is the requested r0, already at scaleResolutionDownBy 4 and the r0 cap from produce() itself. The unit check shows applyProducerBitrateProfile leaves it at that same value ({scaleResolutionDownBy:4,maxBitrate:2520000} in and out), so this function would not be the cause. The defect was not real on the original code either. The function is identical at ac1c688 and has not changed since 4fa0eef (2026-03-26), which added it together with the simulcast produce() call. ac1c688's lockfile has the same mediasoup-client 3.24.5, and the unit check gives the same output on ac1c688's HostView.jsx. No file changed and nothing was committed.

issues.title: Shutdown transport IDs are cleaned up through the wrong event emitter
issues.test: tests/socketTransportShutdownIds.test.js (new; real mediasoup 3.27.1 worker and router, DirectTransports, real socket.io server): 'a receive transport closed when its viewer leaves is dropped from the ignore list', 'receive transports replaced by a new one or closed on disconnect are dropped from the ignore list', 'a host send transport replaced by create-send-transport is dropped from the ignore list', 'destroying a room drops its host and viewer transports from the ignore list', 'transports already closed by their router are not added to the ignore list when the room is destroyed', plus the contract test 'mediasoup reports a closed transport on its observer, not on the transport'
issues.proof: Holds, on the original code too: lib/socket.js at ac1c688 (lines 1115-1134) has the same listener, with mediasoup ^3.27.1. markTransportForShutdown adds the id (lib/socket.js:420) and attachTransportStateHandlers drops it only on transport.on('close') (:1152). mediasoup never emits 'close' on a transport: node_modules/mediasoup/node/lib/Transport.js close() emits '@close' and observer 'close' (:177-179), routerClosed() 'routerclose' and observer 'close' (:213-215), listenServerClosed() 'listenserverclose' and observer 'close' (:253-255). A scratch probe with a real worker printed: WebRtcTransport close() events=["observer:close"], DirectTransport close() events=["observer:close"], router.close() events=["transport:routerclose","observer:close"]. So every socket transport the server closed itself (viewer leave or disconnect, recv transport replaced, host send transport replaced, room destroyed) stayed in the process-wide set until stopJoinCleanup, which runs at startup and in cleanupGlobalResources at shutdown (server.js:1217). On the unchanged code 5 of the 6 new tests failed with 'expected: 0, actual: 1' (leave, replace/disconnect, host replace) and 'expected: 0, actual: 2' (room destroy, router closed first). The existing ignore-list assertions in tests/socketHostSendPath.test.js and tests/socketRecvTransportDeparture.test.js passed only because their fake transports emitted 'close' on themselves, which mediasoup does not. Fix: listen on transport.observer 'close', and skip marking a transport that is already closed (after a router or WebRtcServer close no event follows, so its id would stay). The two fixtures now emit close through an observer as mediasoup does: on the unchanged lib/socket.js 9 of their 17 tests then fail (actual 1), with the fix all pass. Severity is overstated: the ids are random UUIDs that are never reused, so a stale entry changes no behaviour; the cost is memory, about 0.5 KB per id (measured: 100k crypto.randomUUID() strings in a Set on Node 22.14) per transport the server closes, for the life of the process. Checks: touched and related socket test files 39/39; npm run lint and npm run typecheck pass; npm test 999/1000, the one failure tests/portResolver.test.js 'findAvailablePort skips occupied and reserved ports' (ERR_SOCKET_BAD_PORT 65536: the port-0 listener got a port at the top of the range), unrelated, passed 3/3 alone.

issues.title: Cross-worker media-flow file lock leaks its ticket when beforeEach times out, deadlocking every later test
issues.test: tests/mediaFlowLockHooks.test.js (new): 'a media-flow test that times out in beforeEach waiting for the lock leaves nothing that blocks later tests' and 'the media-flow lock lives under the project outputDir, which Playwright clears when a run starts'. They load the real tests/browser/media-flow.spec.mjs with @playwright/test stubbed (a module.register resolve hook) and drive its hooks the way Playwright does, with two module instances standing for two workers. Also a scratch Playwright harness that runs the real spec file with no web server and a planted holder ticket released when the first test ends (dev-notes/results/check-12-playwright.config.mjs.txt, check-12-setup.mjs.txt, check-12-reporter.mjs.txt, check-12-pw-runs.sh; logs check-12-pw-*.log), run with the Playwright lock held.
issues.proof: The claim holds, on the original code too: tests/browser/media-flow.spec.mjs is byte-identical at ac1c688 and dev 1be0088. beforeEach writes its ticket (lines 525-526) and then waits in for(;;) (529-535). The ticket path reaches loopbackProxyState only after the wait and the proxy listen (587-594), and afterEach returns at once when that is null (602). Playwright 1.63 races each hook against the deadline (worker/workerProcessEntry.js:403-406, Promise.race in TimeoutManager.withRunnable), so on a timeout the hook keeps running and its catch (595-598) never runs. afterEach still runs, because shouldRunAfterEachHooks is set before beforeEach (:1644-1645, :1671-1672). Unit test on the unchanged spec: fails with 'afterEach left the timed-out test queued for the lock' (folder [holder ticket, 1792864080580-0000-...ticket] instead of [holder ticket]) and 'the held lock is not under the project outputDir' (check-12-unit-before.txt). Real Playwright, original spec, 4 s timeout, holder ticket released when test 1 ended: all 12 tests 'Test timeout of 4000ms exceeded while running "beforeEach" hook'. One orphan ticket was added per test and 12 were left, although the holder had released at 4.7 s (check-12-pw-before.log). With outputDir moved elsewhere, a stale ticket in <cwd>/test-results was not cleared by the run start and blocked the test (check-12-pw-outdir-before.log). Fix (cf2a56c): the ticket is tracked from the first line of beforeEach, afterEach marks it abandoned and removes it even when beforeEach never finished, the wait loop and the post-listen step stop on 'abandoned', and the lock folder is path.join(testInfo.project.outputDir, '.media-flow-lock'). After the fix both unit tests pass (check-12-unit-after.txt). Dropping the loop's abandoned check makes the first one fail with 'the abandoned beforeEach is still waiting'. Same Playwright scenario with the server and the 60 s timeout: test 1 times out with only the holder ticket left, tests 2-12 pass, and the folder is empty at the end (check-12-pw-after.log). The outputDir scenario passes, with the stale ticket cleared at the run start. The real playwright.config.mjs gives 12 passed (33.0 s). lint, typecheck and npm test (1014/1014) pass. Overstated in the claim: only the chromium project runs this file. Later tests time out one by one (60 s each) rather than hang. A single Ctrl+C or --max-failures interrupts the test and still runs afterEach, so a holder's ticket was freed and only a waiter's leaked (the same path, now fixed). With fullyParallel false and the lock only in this file, a normal run needs a hard-killed worker or real contention (--fully-parallel, --repeat-each with several workers) for the first unreleased ticket. Left for TASK-092: a hard-killed worker's ticket still blocks the rest of that run, because this fix adds no reclamation. The next run starts clean, because the folder is now in outputDir.

issues.title: Asynchronous Blob conversion bypasses relay generation isolation
issues.test: Scratch browser check watch-check13-run.mjs with watch-check13-page/ (lane `watch` scratchpad, Playwright lock held): Vite 8.3.4 bundles a page that imports `io` from socket.io-client and the app's own createSocketOptions() from src/lib/socketOptions.mjs (so the browser field and exports resolve as in the app build); a real socket.io 4.8.4 server emits 'media-chunk' {generation, chunk: Buffer} exactly as lib/socket.js forwards it (toBinaryChunk always yields a Node Buffer), and the page records the chunk's type in onChunk's terms (instanceof Blob / ArrayBuffer). Run in headless Chromium, Firefox and WebKit, each with the app's options (websocket first, tryAllTransports), websocket only and polling only. Output kept in watch-check13-browser-output.txt.
issues.proof: The claim does not hold as a defect. Its reading of the code is right: src/WatchView.jsx:478 checks `payload.generation !== selectedGeneration` before `data.arrayBuffer().then(enqueueChunk)` (484-486), enqueueChunk (438-474) never re-checks the generation or relayCleanupDone, and onMediaInit (501-506) clears the queue and moves selectedGeneration, so a Blob read still pending across a media-init would push old-generation bytes into the new queue. But that branch never runs: Nextra's viewers never receive a Blob. The client never sets binaryType (src/lib/socketOptions.mjs, src/context/SocketContext.jsx), engine.io-client 6.6.6's browser default is 'arraybuffer' (build/esm/globals.js:21 `defaultBinaryType = "arraybuffer"`, mapped over globals.node.js by its browser field; the shipped dist bundle has `ye=`arraybuffer`` and no 'blob'), websocket.js:29 sets `ws.binaryType = this.socket.binaryType`, and engine.io-parser's decodePacket.browser.js mapBinary returns an ArrayBuffer for 'arraybuffer' on every transport (WebSocket frames, base64 long-polling, WebTransport). The browser check confirms it: 27 of 27 chunks arrived as '[object ArrayBuffer]' (isBlob false, engine binaryType 'arraybuffer') in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit over websocket and polling, with the app's options too ('rows=27 blobRows=0 errors=0'). With an ArrayBuffer, onChunk takes the synchronous branch (490-491) and enqueueChunk runs in the same task as the generation check, so no media-init can come between them, and nothing is left running for cleanup to cancel. issues.title: Hardcoded DTLS setup:passive in WHEP answer causes handshake deadlock when viewer offers passive
issues.test: tests/whep.test.js, describe 'WHEP answer a=setup matches the DTLS role given to mediasoup': "answers a=setup:active in every section for a <session|media>-level a=setup:passive offer, with remote role 'server'" (both failed before the fix); "reads the offered setup value case-insensitively (ABNF strings, RFC 5234 section 2.3)" (failed before); "takes one a=setup for every section from the section that supplies the DTLS parameters" (failed before); the actpass, active and no-setup cases (5 tests) passed before and after. Real-mediasoup check: results/check-17-dtls-probe.js (output in results/check-17-probe-output.txt)
issues.proof: The defect holds, though not by the mechanism the claim gives. lib/whep.js parseViewerDtls (line 195 at 109f819, the same at ac1c688) gives transport.connect() remote role 'server' for a=setup:passive, while buildActiveSection (line 531 at 109f819, line 373 at ac1c688) always wrote a=setup:passive. The claim says neither side then sends a ClientHello. That part is wrong: the probe (mediasoup 3.27.1 worker, WebRtcTransport connected as lib/whepRoutes.js does it, ICE completed with a hand-built STUN binding request) shows that for a passive offer mediasoup takes local role 'client' and sends a DTLS ClientHello (5 packets, with retransmits), and for actpass, active or no setup it takes 'server' and sends nothing. What is wrong is the answer. It said passive while mediasoup acted as client, and RFC 4145 section 4.1 allows only active (or holdconn) as the answer to a passive offer. A viewer that follows the answer also becomes DTLS client (two clients, no handshake); a strict one rejects the answer. Only a viewer that ignores the answer's setup worked. Browsers offer actpass (JSEP), so the case is non-browser WHEP clients that offer passive, which the code meant to support. The probe gave the same result on lib/whep.js from ac1c688, so the original code had the defect too. Before the fix, node --test --test-name-pattern=a=setup tests/whep.test.js: 4 of 9 new tests failed, e.g. expected setups ['active','active'], actual ['passive','passive'] with role 'server'. Fix: one helper, viewerDtlsRoles, gives both the remote role and the answer's a=setup (passive -> 'server'/active, anything else -> 'client'/passive), read case-insensitively from the video (else audio) section, one value for every answered section. After the fix the probe shows answer a=setup:active for the passive offer, matching mediasoup's client role, and the other answers unchanged. tests/whep.test.js 121/121; npm run lint, npm run typecheck pass; npm test 1060/1060. Commit a863cb6 on lane/netcheck.

issues.title: Configuration rollback restarts OBS stream after setup failure
issues.test: Scratch probe .arbitra/dev-notes/results/check-18-probe.mjs (output in check-18-probe-output.txt): a fake OBS WebSocket with real state (the stream follows StartStream/StopStream, the service follows SetStreamServiceSettings) runs configureObsStream from the lane's src/lib/obsWebSocket.js (dev 4daa571) and from a copy of ac1c688's src/lib/obsWebSocket.js + obsOutputModel.mjs, in five cases: OBS idle and setup fails (no AV1 encoder); OBS live at its own target and setup fails (no AV1 encoder); OBS live and an auto-start the WHIP target refuses; OBS retrying an earlier target and setup fails; OBS live and the video settings refused. Plus the existing tests that pin the restart, 'OBS configuration rollback restores mutations in reverse order', 'a rollback starts the stream again only after the video settle time has passed since the last video restore' and 'a video color restore counts for the settle time, ...' (node --test tests/obsWebSocket.test.js tests/obsWebSocketWire.test.js: 52/52 pass).
issues.proof: The mechanism the claim describes is right, the defect is not: the restart is the rollback restoring the stream OBS had before the setup, by design. configureObsStream does stop through the transaction (src/lib/obsWebSocket.js:812 stopActiveStream(sendRequest), sendRequest = transaction.request at :766; ac1c688 :579), the StopStream is journaled with a StartStream inverse (:514-519, :641, :668; ac1c688 :490-493) and a failed setup replays it (:678). But it is journaled first, so it is replayed last, after the previous stream service, video and profile values are restored: what restarts is the user's own earlier stream at its own target, not a broadcast to the Nextra room. The probe shows it on both versions: OBS live at rtmp://live.example/app, setup fails for want of an AV1 encoder -> 'StopStream (was active at rtmp://live.example/app) | GetStreamServiceSettings | SetStreamServiceSettings -> http://127.0.0.1:8889/whip/ROOM | SetStreamServiceSettings -> rtmp://live.example/app | StartStream at rtmp://live.example/app', result 'No AV1 OBS encoders were configured for this host. OBS settings were restored. ...', before and after 'stream active at rtmp://live.example/app'; with an auto-start the WHIP target refuses the end state is the same; with OBS idle no StartStream is replayed and OBS ends idle. That the restart is intended is in the code and the owner's own text: the transaction's doc (:528-540) and streamInverse ('Starting the stream undoes stopping it'), the test-stream comment that only Nextra's own start/stop pair is housekeeping that 'a failed setup' should not roll back (:838-841; ac1c688 :606-608), src/HostView.jsx:1555-1557, written in Release 2.1.0 before the audit (ac1c688 :1463-1465): 'a failed run can still leave OBS streaming (rollback restarts it)', with a control channel opened for exactly that stream, and audits-codex/REMAINING-WORK.md at a7d610b (:114-117) 'snapshots stream service, video, profile, output, and stream-state mutations, restores them in reverse order after a later failure'. This plan's TASK-079 built on it (a stop gate and the 1200 ms settle before 'a StartStream inverse'), and its tests above pin it. Sending the stop raw, as the claim implies, would make a failed setup end the user's live broadcast for good. The claim's examples are also partly wrong: a wrong OBS password fails at Identify, before the setup callback runs (:184, :212-214, the callback is called only on op 2 at :222-235), so nothing is stopped; a refused resolution is only a warning (:848-855) and commits (probe: success=true, 'Warnings: resolution (invalid resolution)'). Only setup failures (no usable encoder, encoder not verified, x264 for AV1, auto-start failed or stopped at once), an exception and the deadline roll back. Original code: same journaling and order at ac1c688, so not a defect there either; the only difference in the probe is the auto-start case, where ac1c688 added 'Rollback incomplete: StopStream: not active' (fixed by TASK-079, a different issue). No file changed.

issues.title: A new relay generation mid-playback is appended to the existing SourceBuffer without abort() or changeType()
issues.test: tests/browser/media-flow.spec.mjs: 'a playing relay viewer follows the host recorder from MP4 to VP8' and 'a relay viewer that is behind keeps playing across a VP8 recorder restart' (Playwright, Chromium, real server and host; both failed on the unchanged build and pass on the fix, 3 of 3 repeats); tests/watchPlaybackMode.test.js: 'a new relay generation on a playing SourceBuffer resets its parser first', 'a new relay generation in another format switches the SourceBuffer type after the reset', 'a SourceBuffer that cannot take the new relay generation is reported, not reused'. Probe: .arbitra/dev-notes/results/check-19-mse-probe.cjs.txt with check-19-mse-probe-page.js.txt (real MediaRecorder + MSE in Chromium 153 and Firefox 155), output check-19-mse-probe-output.txt
issues.proof: The claim is about src/WatchView.jsx startRelayPlayback (the browser-host MediaRecorder relay: onMediaInit, selectedGeneration, WebM/EBML), not src/lib/fmp4RelayPlayer.js; WatchView.jsx is byte-identical at ac1c688, and the host restart logic (HostView.jsx 1262-1301: frame rate, resolution, bitrate and the MP4-to-VP8 fallback all restart the recorder) and the server relay are unchanged, so it was real on the original code too. onMediaInit (WatchView.jsx 497-513 before the fix) flushes the queue and moves selectedGeneration and mimeType but leaves the SourceBuffer as it was: no abort(), no changeType(). Two failures follow. (1) Chromium's MediaRecorder ends every timeslice one byte into the next WebM element (EBML walk of recorded bytes: all 9 and 12 chunk ends at '+1' into a SimpleBlock, BlockGroup or Cluster), so when old-generation chunks are still queued at the new media-init and flushed, the parser is left inside an element: in the probe the SourceBuffer then took all 13 appends of the new generation and buffered none of them (buffered stuck at [0,2.42], no error event, MediaSource open, no video error); with abort() it buffered to 6.1 s. (2) MP4 to VP8 (lib/socket.js onError emits relay-mp4-failed and expects viewers to 'pick up' the new generation; HostView's MP4 recorder.onerror does the same): the MP4 SourceBuffer swallowed the VP8 generation the same way (buffered stuck at 2.94 s); with abort()+changeType() it reached 7.04 s. The claim's consequence is slightly off: Chromium raises no parse error and does not end the MediaSource; the picture freezes silently and the queue never overflows, so no error is shown either. Firefox's recorder cuts at element boundaries, so Firefox-recorded VP8 survives the flush. E2E on the unchanged build (check-19-e2e-before.txt): MP4 to VP8 'Expected: > 4.528974 Received: 3.148159' (video frozen after the switch), viewer behind across a frame-rate restart 'Expected: > 4.4882919999999995 Received: 1.488292'. Fix (commit 231a8f8 on lane/client): new prepareSourceBufferForGeneration(sourceBuffer, mediaSource, {fromMimeType, toMimeType}) in src/lib/watchPlaybackMode.mjs calls abort() and, when the type changes, changeType(); WatchView's onMediaInit calls it once this attempt has a SourceBuffer and, if it returns false (MediaSource not open, no changeType, or the browser refuses the type), ends the attempt through failRelayGeneration with RELAY_PLAYBACK_UNSUPPORTED_MESSAGE or 'Relay playback could not follow the new stream and must be restarted.'. Both e2e tests pass after it (check-19-e2e-after.txt). The unit tests failed before only because the helper did not exist. Checks: npm run lint and npm run typecheck clean; npm test 1054/1054; npx playwright test --workers=1: 62 passed, 13 skipped, 3 failed, the 3 tests of tests/browser/host-obs-control-channel.spec.mjs, which fail the same way on the unchanged build (also in check-19-e2e-before.txt). src/lib/fmp4RelayPlayer.js (OBS fMP4 relay) does not have this defect: handleMediaInit calls changeType through switchSourceBufferType or rebuilds the MediaSource, and its chunks are whole moof+mdat fragments (lib/fmp4Parser.js), so its parser is always at a box boundary.

issues.test: Scratch check socket-check-20-handshake.js (lane `socket` scratchpad), run on dev bfe4d26 and on an archive of ac1c688: (1) a real socket.io 4.8.4 server with registerSocketHandlers(io, {}, {}), so the default resolver getSocketIp is used, records socket.handshake in io.use() middleware and in 'connection', then a websocket client and a polling client each emit join-room {code:'ABCDEF'}; (2) a hand-made socket with no handshake fed to registerSocketHandlers through a fake io, with the default resolver and with a resolver that never reads handshake. issues.title: Cumulative RTP timestamp delta exceeds signed 32-bit limit and permanently drops audio
issues.test: tests/oggOpusMuxer.test.js: 'Ogg granules keep following the RTP clock past 2^31 samples' (also 'Ogg granules stay correct when the 32-bit RTP timestamp wraps', 'Ogg muxer still drops late and duplicate packets after the 2^31 horizon', 'Ogg muxer measures the 2^31 limit from the last accepted packet', 'Ogg muxer re-anchors to the current granule on an SSRC change', 'Ogg muxer starts from a preset granule and keeps counting from it', 'Ogg muxer keeps its anchor unset until a packet is accepted')
issues.proof: Holds. OggOpusMuxer.pushRtp set baseTimestamp only on the first packet or an SSRC change and measured every delta as (timestamp - baseTimestamp) >>> 0 from there, rejecting anything above 0x7fffffff, so once a stream ran 2^31 samples (about 12.4 h at 48 kHz, sooner with a large first timestamp) every packet read as 'backwards' and was dropped for good; past 2^32 samples the delta wrapped back to a small number and a packet would have got a granule far behind the stream. The new test sends packets 2^30 samples apart (5000, 5000+2^30, ...); on the unchanged code it failed with: "packet 2 at 2147483648 samples after the first was dropped" (expected true, actual null), and the same shape failed in the 2^32 wrap test ("packet 3 after the 2^32 total was dropped") and in the preset-granule test ("packet 2 after the preset granule was dropped"); the late/duplicate, 0x7fffffff limit and SSRC tests failed the same way at the first packet more than 2^31 samples after the first. Fix: after a packet is accepted the muxer re-anchors on it (baseTimestamp = its timestamp, baseGranule = its granule minus its duration), so the unsigned 32-bit delta is always the gap to the last accepted packet; rejected packets never move the anchor; an SSRC change still re-anchors to the current granule; the page is built before any state is committed, so a packet that cannot be written (the one-page size limit throws) no longer leaves baseTimestamp set (the last test failed on the old code for that reason: baseTimestamp was 4000, expected null). All 15 muxer tests pass after the fix, including the 8 existing ones, and the FFmpeg test (tests/oggOpusFfmpeg.test.js, real FFmpeg) still passes.

issues.title: RTP sequence gap detection occurs after frame emission on timestamp transition
issues.test: tests/h264Depacketizer.test.js: 'VAL-003: a lost marker packet flags the damaged frame, not its successor' (also 'VAL-004 (a): one packet missing where a frame never saw its marker damages only that frame', 'VAL-004 (b): more than one packet missing where a frame never saw its marker damages both frames', 'VAL-004 (c): packets missing after a frame that closed on its marker damage the next frame', 'VAL-004 (d): a gap inside a frame, with no timestamp change, damages that frame', and the guards 'pushFrames keeps a frame intact when its marker is missing but no packet is', 'pushFrames counts a sequence number wrap as contiguous and a gap across it as missing', 'a frame whose fragments vanish at a lost marker still marks the following frame')
issues.proof: Holds. pushFrames called _emitFrame at a timestamp change before it compared the sequence number with the previous packet, so a gap that fell at that boundary was applied to the frame that starts there instead of the one that lost the packet. VAL-003 loses the marker packet of a two-packet frame (sequence 1 at timestamp 3000, sequence 2 lost, then sequence 3 at 6000 with its marker); on the unchanged code it failed with the pair swapped: expected [[3000, false], [6000, true]], actual [[3000, true], [6000, false]]. VAL-004 (a) (one lost packet at an unterminated transition) failed with the damaged frame 6000 emitted as intact (expected false, actual true), and VAL-004 (b) (two lost packets, so the new frame may have lost its head too) failed the same way for the pending frame 6000; VAL-004 (c) (gap after a frame closed on its marker) and (d) (gap inside a frame) passed before and after, as did the vanished-frame, marker-less and sequence-wrap guards, and are kept to pin those behaviours. Fix: pushFrames computes missing = (sequence - lastSequence - 1) & 0xffff first. At a timestamp change with a pending frame (no marker seen) it marks the pending frame not intact when missing >= 1, emits it, and marks the new frame not intact only when missing > 1 (Q-005 default). Otherwise any gap marks the current frame, or the frame that starts here after one closed on its marker. A pending frame that holds nothing usable still carries the flag to the next frame. One departure from the prompt's wording: step 2 reads as marking the pending frame whenever the marker is absent, but with no packet missing nothing was lost, and senders that never set the marker bit would then have every frame reported as damaged, so the pending frame is marked only when packets are missing (the existing test 'pushFrames ends a frame at the next timestamp when the marker never came' and the new marker-less guard cover it). All 11 existing tests in the file pass unchanged.

issues.title: H.264 reassembly has no aggregate memory limit
issues.test: tests/h264Depacketizer.test.js: 'VAL-005: a fragmented NAL over the byte limit is dropped instead of growing without end' (also 'VAL-005: a fragmented NAL over the fragment limit is dropped', 'VAL-005: a frame whose NAL overflows is dropped, its packets are skipped, and the next frame is flagged', 'VAL-005: an access unit over the byte limit is dropped even when no marker ever arrives', 'VAL-005: the marker of an oversized frame ends the skipping', 'VAL-005: an access unit over the packet limit is dropped', 'VAL-005: a fragmented NAL in progress counts toward the access unit limit', and the boundary and option guards 'VAL-005: a fragmented NAL at exactly the byte limit is still reassembled', 'VAL-005: an access unit at exactly the byte limit is emitted whole', 'VAL-005: invalid limit options fall back to the defaults')
issues.proof: Holds. _fuBuffer (FU-A continuations) and _frameChunks (complete NALs of one timestamp) had no byte, packet or time limit, so a peer that never sent an FU-A end bit, or never sent a marker and kept one timestamp, grew them for ever. The new tests inject small limits (no large allocations). On the unchanged code the options were ignored and: the 3-fragment, 61-byte FU-A with maxNalBytes 50 still reassembled at its end packet (expected 0 bytes, actual 70); 4 fragments with maxFragments 3 still reassembled (expected 0, actual 10); the pushFrames frame with an oversized NAL was emitted at its marker instead of being dropped; packets at one timestamp with maxAccessUnitBytes 100 kept being held past the limit (assertion held chunks stay within the limit failed), likewise with maxFragments 3; and an in-progress FU-A stayed in memory after the access unit passed its limit (_fuBuffer was not null). Fix: constructor options maxNalBytes (default 8 MiB), maxAccessUnitBytes (16 MiB) and maxFragments (32768, applied to the FU-A fragments of one NAL and to the packets of one access unit); invalid values fall back to the defaults. Running counters (_fuBytes, _frameBytes, the chunk count) are checked after every packet. A FU-A over a limit is dropped (its later fragments then match nothing); in pushFrames an access unit over a limit, counting the FU-A in progress, is dropped whole, _frameIntact is set false so the next frame is reported as damaged, and the remaining packets of that timestamp are skipped until its marker or the next timestamp. A scratch run with the defaults held at most 32768 packets, 32768 fragments and 8,388,001 FU bytes after 200000, 200000 and 20000 packets. issues.title: Fragmented SPS/PPS prefixes are cached as complete parameter sets
issues.test: tests/h264Sprop.test.js: 'collectParameterSets does not cache a FU-A start fragment of an SPS or PPS' (also 'a complete SPS/PPS after a FU-A start fragment replaces nothing and is captured'; guards 'extractNalUnits still reports a FU-A start fragment with its original NAL type', 'extractNalUnits ignores FU-A continuation and end fragments', 'collectParameterSets keeps the first complete SPS/PPS and ignores later fragments')
issues.proof: Holds. extractNalUnits pushed the FU-A start fragment of a NAL (its rebuilt NAL header plus the bytes of that one packet) as an ordinary entry, and collectParameterSets cached the first type-7 and type-8 entry it saw, so a fragmented SPS or PPS was taken as complete and, because the capture keeps the first value, a later complete copy could never replace it (lib/whipRoutes.js builds the sprop-parameter-sets and the stored SPS/PPS from it). The new tests build FU-A start packets of type 7 and 8 and feed them through extractNalUnits and extractNalUnitsFromRtp. On the unchanged code 'does not cache a FU-A start fragment' failed with the truncated SPS returned (expected { sps: null, pps: null }, actual sps = 67 42 e0 1f), and 'a complete SPS/PPS after a FU-A start fragment' failed with the 4-byte fragment kept instead of the complete 7-byte SPS (expected 67 42 e0 1f 8c 8d 40, actual 67 42 e0 1f); the three guard tests passed before and after and pin that the FU-A start entry is still returned with its original NAL type (IDR 5, SPS 7) and that continuation and end fragments are ignored. Fix in lib/h264Sprop.js: extractNalUnits records each FU-A start fragment it returns in a module-level WeakSet, and collectParameterSets skips entries in it, so a truncated parameter set is never cached and a later complete one (single NAL or STAP-A, in the same batch or a later packet with the accumulator threaded through) is captured. The array extractNalUnits returns is unchanged, so lib/whipRoutes.js, the only caller of extractNalUnitsFromRtp and collectParameterSets, still sees the start fragment's type for its nalTypesSeen log; the other importers (lib/h264Depacketizer.js, lib/oggOpusMuxer.js, lib/socket.js) use only rtpPayloadOffset and profileLevelIdFromInitSegment, which are unchanged. A fragmented SPS/PPS is still not reassembled, so a stream that only ever fragments its parameter sets stays uncaptured and the 12 s capture times out as before (full reassembly is out of scope). The mark is by object identity: a caller that copied the buffers before collectParameterSets would lose it; none does.

issues.title: FFmpegRelay.restart() and start() can respawn FFmpeg after the owner has called stop()
issues.test: tests/ffmpegRelay.test.js: 'an owner stop() during the restart backoff keeps FFmpeg stopped (VAL-011)', 'an owner stop() from an exit listener keeps FFmpeg stopped (VAL-011)', 'an owner stop() while start() awaits the encoder probes prevents the spawn (VAL-011)' (guard: 'the relay's own stop() and a reconfigure never trigger a restart (VAL-011, VAL-012)')

issues.title: Immediate reset of _stdinCap in writeVideoFrame defeats burst buffer expansion
issues.test: tests/ffmpegRelay.test.js: 'a replayed GOP of the declared size is written whole to a fresh process (VAL-013)', 'the normal cap and the video-gap return once the burst has been written and has drained (VAL-013)', 'a burst that is declared but not yet written keeps its allowance while stdin is empty (VAL-013)' (guard: 'stop() and a new start() clear an unfinished burst allowance (VAL-013)')
issues.proof: Holds. writeVideoFrame() ran `if (writableLength <= MAX_STDIN_BUFFERED_BYTES) _stdinCap = MAX_STDIN_BUFFERED_BYTES` before every write, and a fresh process starts with an empty stdin, so the cap beginBurst() had raised (4 MiB + 2x the burst) was thrown away by the first frame of the burst; the frames after it were dropped once the queue passed 4 MiB, and the next frame after a drain raised 'video-gap'. On the unchanged code: writing ten 1 MiB frames after beginBurst(10 MiB) failed with 'frame 4 of the burst' (false !== true) because writableLength 4 MiB + 48 bytes was over the restored 4 MiB cap; the second test failed on the same drop; the third (8 MiB declared, two 1 MiB frames written, then the queue at 9 MiB) failed on the third frame. The existing test 'a replayed GOP is not mistaken for FFmpeg falling behind' declares 10 MiB, writes 64 bytes and then drains the stub queue, which the prompt's rule would keep at the raised cap, so the allowance also ends when stdin was seen above the normal cap since beginBurst() and is back under it (`_burstBackedUp`). start(), stop() and the restart/reconfigure teardown call `_resetBurst()`; beginBurst() ignores a non-finite size. issues.title: consume lets one viewer create unlimited consumers of the same producer (egress amplification)
issues.test: tests/socketConsumeLimits.test.js: 'repeated consume of one producer leaves one live consumer and closes the superseded ones', 'a viewer keeps one live consumer for each producer, video and audio', 'overlapping consume calls for one producer converge on the newest consumer', 'overlapping consume calls finishing out of order still leave exactly one live consumer', 'consume closes its new consumer when the receive transport was replaced during the await', 'consume closes its new consumer when the receive transport was closed during the await', 'consume closes its new consumer when the room was destroyed during the await', 'consuming a new producer id after a producer change still succeeds'
issues.proof: Holds. consume always created a consumer and pushed it to viewerData.consumers, and never looked at the consumers the viewer already had for that producerId. The new tests (tests/socketConsumeLimits.test.js, eight; seven failed on the unchanged code, one guards unchanged behaviour) drive a real socket.io server with a host and a viewer and a fake receive transport whose consumers behave like mediasoup's (close() is idempotent and fires the observer). On the unchanged code: six sequential consume calls for one producer left six consumers in viewerData.consumers (strictEqual 6 !== 1; the test stops at that assertion, the close() and consumer-resume assertions after it were not reached on the unchanged code); three rounds of video+audio left six (6 !== 2); two overlapping calls (deferred recvTransport.consume) left both (deepEqual against [newer] failed), three overlapping calls finishing out of order left three (3 !== 1); and when create-recv-transport, close-viewer-transport or destroyRoom ran during the awaited consume, the consume still answered success and kept the new consumer on the stale viewer (true !== false in each). Fix (lib/socket.js, consume handler): the receive transport is read once before the await; after the two awaits the handler checks that the socket is still in the same room, room.viewerTransports.get(socket.id) is the same viewerData and its recvTransport is the same transport, and otherwise closes the new consumer and answers 'No recv transport.' (counted in consumeDenied, never in consumesCreated or activeConsumerIds); otherwise it counts, pushes and attaches the listeners as before and then closes every other consumer of that viewer with the same producerId (try/catch each, removeConsumerFromViewer, activeConsumerIds.delete) before the callback, so overlapping calls end with the last one to finish and the list holds at most one consumer per active room producer (two). Callback params, paused creation, consumer-resume and the metric names are unchanged. No separate per-viewer cap was added; the dedupe bounds the list because producerId is limited to the room's active producers. After the fix all eight pass; node --test tests/socketConsumeLimits.test.js 8/8, npm run lint, npm run typecheck and npm test (500/500) pass.

issues.title: createViewerAnswer allocates consumers to rejected/inactive SDP offer sections
issues.test: tests/whep.test.js, describe 'createViewerAnswer section eligibility': 'gives the video consumer to the active video section when a disabled (port 0) one comes first'; 'gives the audio consumer to the active audio section when an a=inactive one comes first'; 'answers every section as rejected, with no BUNDLE group, when all sections are disabled or inactive'; 'does not give a consumer to a section the viewer only sends on (sendonly)'; 'omits a=mid from a rejected section when the offer had no mid for it'
issues.proof: Holds. createViewerAnswer looked up consumersByKind[section.kind] for every parsed m-section and deleted the entry on the first match, without looking at the section's port or direction, so a port-0 or a=inactive section ahead of an active one of the same kind took the consumer and was answered with port 9 (and its mid in BUNDLE), while the active section after it fell through to the rejected branch. On the unchanged code, 5 of the 8 new tests failed: the disabled-video-first test with "section should be rejected with port 0: m=video 9 UDP/TLS/RTP/SAVPF 96" (the port-0 section was answered as active), the inactive-audio-first test with the same message for m=audio 9, and the all-disabled test with the same message (every section was active although none was offered). The sendonly test and the no-mid test failed with the same message (a sendonly section and a port-0 section were answered active). Before the fix a rejected section also always printed a made-up a=mid (default '0' or '1', so two rejected video sections shared a mid); the no-mid test pins that, but the port-0 failure came first. The other 3 new tests (no direction attribute counts as sendrecv, an eligible section with no consumer left is rejected in place with its mid, one active section per kind gives an unchanged answer) pass before and after; they guard the behaviour the fix must keep. Fix (lib/whep.js): a new isOfferSectionEligible(section) accepts a section only when port !== 0 and the direction is recvonly or sendrecv (a missing direction is sendrecv, the parser's default); createViewerAnswer gives a consumer only to eligible sections, so the first eligible section of a kind gets it and every other section is answered in place with port 0, a=inactive and its offered a=mid, excluded from a=group:BUNDLE (section-189067a43c5f50160f1b8635/Q-005 default); buildRejectedSection prints a=mid only when the offer had one. The new tests check that the answer has as many m-lines as the offer, in the same order, with the consumer's ssrc and the offered mid on the active section. issues.proof: On the unchanged code the leave-room, moved-room and destroyed-room tests got success: true instead of { success: false, error: 'Not in a room.' } for a transport allocated after the viewer was gone, and the disconnect test timed out waiting for the stale transport to be closed (it was stored in room.viewerTransports instead). After the fix create-recv-transport, once the allocation resolves and its state handlers are attached, requires socket.connected !== false, findRoomBySocket(socket.id) === room and findRoomByCode(room.code) === room; otherwise it marks the transport for shutdown, closes it, answers { success: false, error: 'Not in a room.' } and stores nothing. All four pass, the allocated transport is closed and absent from room.viewerTransports, and the ignored-transport count returns to its baseline (__testing.getIgnoredTransportCount). 'create-recv-transport stores the transport and succeeds for a viewer that stays' and the two overlapping-call tests (existing raced-transport cleanup) pass before and after.

With a fake child (EventEmitter, PassThrough stdout and stderr) writing 'https://abc-' and then 'def.trycloudflare.com', the launch never resolved and 8 tests failed with 'the launch is still waiting for a public URL' (split over stdout, over stderr, cut at the domain suffix, one-character chunks, lowercase variant, URL after a large log, timeout-cleared test, debug-logging test). issues.title: Rotated startup logs escape retention cleanup
issues.test: tests/startupLogRetention.test.js: 'pruning removes the .log, .log.1 and .log.2 of every session beyond the newest ten', 'the newest ten sessions keep every generation', 'a pruned session whose primary file is already gone loses its leftover generations', 'sessions that rotated a different number of times are grouped by their stem', 'startup-latest.log, its generations and unrelated files are never pruned', 'ten sessions or fewer, including rotated ones, are all kept', 'the keep option sets how many sessions stay', 'the session pattern captures the stem and an optional numeric generation', 'an empty or missing log directory is a no-op', 'pruning failures are swallowed and the other files are still removed', 'lib/startupRuntime.js prunes with the helper when it starts' (a child process with NEXTRA_LOG_DIR pointing at a temporary directory), 'the helper ships with the packaged app: it sits in lib/, which the packager copies whole, and needs only Node'
issues.proof: Run against the unchanged pruning logic (moved verbatim into lib/startupLogRetention.js so a test can load it; lib/startupRuntime.js cannot be required because it patches process.stdout/stderr on load): with 13 sessions of .log, .log.1 and .log.2 in a temporary directory, the 3 oldest sessions lost only their .log and kept .log.1 and .log.2 ('startup-20200101-120000-4001.log.1 should have been pruned with its session'); a session whose .log was already gone was never touched; and the real lib/startupRuntime.js run in a child process with 12 such sessions left the oldest two sessions' rotated files behind (same message). 5 of the 13 tests failed for that reason (4 more failed only because the verbatim extraction takes no keep option and returns no list of removed names). issues.title: uncaughtExceptionMonitor shows a synchronous 15-second PowerShell modal, even for exceptions the app may recover from, and reports runtime crashes as startup failures
issues.test: tests/startupFailureReporter.test.js, run against the real lib/startupRuntime.js in a child process: 'an uncaught exception that an uncaughtException listener handles logs a line but shows no dialog' and 'exit code 0 shows no dialog, also after a handled exception' (both failed before the fix), 'a fatal uncaught exception still exits non-zero and shows one dialog that does not claim a startup failure' (failed before), and the passing-before regression guards 'a recovering listener that exits 1 after logging, as server.js does, shows exactly one dialog', 'a non-zero exit without any exception shows one dialog with the exit code', 'off Windows nothing is shown, but the exception is still logged and the exit code is unchanged'; plus unit tests of installFailureReporter with a fake EventEmitter and an injected notifier (no notify for a handled exception, exactly one for a non-zero exit, none for exit code 0 or off Windows), of formatFailureMessage and createDialogNotifier, a real-process test that a fatal exception still emits 'exit' with a non-zero code and the notifier runs once from exit, and a packaging test
issues.proof: The unchanged lib/startupRuntime.js was run in a child process (node -r preload -r lib/startupRuntime.js scenario.js) with a preload that sets process.platform to 'win32' and replaces child_process.execFileSync with a recorder, so no real PowerShell dialog opens. With an 'uncaughtException' listener that swallows a thrown error and the process then exiting 0, the recorder saw one powershell.exe Popup call, text 'Nextra could not start correctly.' plus the stack, title 'Nextra startup failed' (the monitor called showFailureDialog; in the real app that is a 15 s synchronous execFileSync that freezes the event loop). A fatal uncaught exception produced the same 'could not start correctly' wording although the process may have run for hours. 3 of 6 child-process tests failed for those reasons (output: .arbitra/dev-notes/results/TASK-032-before.txt). After the fix the monitor in lib/startupFailureReporter.js (installFailureReporter(processLike, { notify, platform, log, getFallbackText })) only writes the log line synchronously and remembers the formatted error; the exit handler writes 'process exit code', and for a non-zero code on win32 calls notify once with { code, summary } where summary is the remembered error, else the last stderr lines, else empty. The dialog text is 'Nextra stopped unexpectedly (exit code N).' plus the error and 'Startup log: <latest path>', the Popup title is 'Nextra stopped'. No startup-complete signal reaches lib/startupRuntime.js (server.js keeps serviceReady to itself and may not change), so the wording does not claim a startup failure (section-189067a43c5f50160f1b8635/Q-004 default). Exit codes are unchanged (the child tests assert 1 and 3). 19 tests pass; the full suite passes. The packaged build needs no package-app.js change: scripts/package-app.js copies 'lib' as a directory and hashes it into the build identifier, and a test pins that. The real packager was not run.

issues.title: DTLS role inverted for non-actpass setup attributes in WHIP ingest
issues.test: tests/whip.test.js: "WHIP remote DTLS role is '<role>' for a <media|session>-level a=setup:<value> offer" (active and passive failed before the fix; actpass and absent passed before and after); "WHIP answer says a=setup:<value> in every section for a <level>-level a=setup:<value> offer, matching remote role '<role>'" (active and passive failed before the fix); "WHIP answer takes one a=setup from the section that supplies the DTLS parameters, for every section" (failed before); "WHIP answer for a setup:actpass offer is unchanged apart from the o= line" (golden captured from the unchanged serializer; passed before and after)
issues.proof: Before the fix, node --test tests/whip.test.js ran 36 tests with 9 failures. parseDtlsParameters returned role 'server' for a=setup:active at media and session level (expected 'client') and 'client' for a=setup:passive at both levels (expected 'server'); createAnswer said a=setup:passive for every offer, so a passive offer got a passive answer and a client-role connect(), the deadlock the issue describes. issues.title: Asynchronous startup can publish a superseded session
issues.test: tests/whipRoutes.test.js: "a WHIP start aborted while transport.connect() is pending gives its transport up at once", "a WHIP start aborted while transport.connect() is pending publishes no session when connect() completes", "a stale transport.connect() completion after a replacement WHIP start leaves the replacement session as it is", "a stale video produce() completion closes only its own producer and never touches the replacement session", "a stale audio produce() completion closes only its own producer and never touches the replacement session", "a WHIP offer without a DTLS fingerprint gets 400 and leaves no transport on the room or in its media pipeline"
issues.proof: The tests run the real WHIP router on a real HTTP server with fake mediasoup transports whose connect()/produce() wait on deferred promises. As in mediasoup 3.27.1, the fake's close() drops its dtlsstatechange listeners without emitting, and a connect() or produce() already pending still resolves afterwards (Transport.close() removes the channel subscription and does not reject pending requests; the worker answers them in order). With the unchanged lib/whipRoutes.js all six failed: after a client abort during connect(), room.whipTransport still pointed at the closed transport and the pipeline still owned it; when that connect() resolved, the cancelled start set whipSessionId ('a3763d11f726b865' !== null) and registered a WHIP resource with no client; after an abort and a replacement POST, the stale connect() overwrote room.whipTransport with the closed transport-1 (so the replacement's DTLS 'connected' would have been ignored); a stale video or audio produce() completing after an OBS reconnect called ownWhip('video-producer'|'audio-producer', staleProducer), which closed the replacement's producer, and then nulled the room field; the 400 for a missing fingerprint left room.whipTransport on the closed transport. After the fix: an isCurrentStart() check (not cancelled, room.whipGeneration and room.whipTransport still this start's) runs after connect() and publishes nothing otherwise; releaseWhipTransport() clears room.whipTransport and the pipeline's ownership together in cancelPendingStart, the post-connect check, the 500 path and the missing-fingerprint 400; commitProducer() assigns a produce() result and calls ownWhip() only while the session is current and DTLS connected, else closes only that producer. node --test tests/whipRoutes.test.js 17/17; tests/roomMediaPipeline.test.js 12/12; npm test 1061/1061; lint and typecheck pass.

issues.title: Producer creation failure after DTLS connect is only logged, leaving a half-initialized session that never goes live and is never torn down
issues.test: tests/whipRoutes.test.js: "a rejected video produce() tears the WHIP session down instead of leaving it half started", "a rejected audio produce() after the video producer tears the whole WHIP session down, video producer included", "DTLS failing while produce() is pending leaves the session disconnected, and the grace timer then closes it" (node:test mock timers); baseline "WHIP happy path: 201, then DTLS connected creates both producers and goes live" passes before and after
issues.proof: With the unchanged lib/whipRoutes.js the three tests failed: after a rejected video produce(), and after a rejected audio produce() following a successful video one, the transport was still open ('the transport is closed': false !== true), the resource stayed registered and the video producer stayed owned by the pipeline; the error was only logged. With DTLS 'failed' emitted while the video produce() was pending, the later completion set room.whipConnected = true (true !== false), emitted new-producer events and prewarmed the relay, so the grace timer would have found a connected session and never closed it. After the fix the connected branch's catch calls teardownGeneration('producer creation failed'), the one generation-scoped helper (also used at grace expiry): when the session is still current it stops the relay, runs closeWhipSession (producers, transport and resource released), sets fallbackAvailable false and emits host metrics; a stale generation does nothing. The tests assert the transport and every producer closed, room fields null, the resource unregistered, the pipeline owning no WHIP transport or producer, whipConnected false, the last host-metrics call made after the teardown, and no new-producer event or relay prewarm. whipConnected is set only if the generation is current and DTLS is still connected after every await; after the DTLS failure the late producer is closed and the mocked grace timer then tears the session down. The added guard on the DTLS failed/closed branch and the grace-timer callback (current generation and transport only) has no test: mediasoup never emits dtlsstatechange for a transport the server closed (check 08), so a stale transport cannot reach that branch.

issues.title: WHIP session liveness depends only on DTLS state, so an abrupt OBS loss or a never-completed ICE leaves the session 'connected' indefinitely
issues.test: tests/whipRoutes.test.js (node:test mock timers): "ICE disconnecting while DTLS stays connected starts the grace period, and the grace timer then closes the session", "ICE returning to 'connected' within the grace period cancels the teardown and restores the connected state", "ICE returning to 'completed' within the grace period cancels the teardown and restores the connected state", "a second ICE outage after a recovery starts a new grace period", "ICE disconnecting while produce() is pending still lets the session go live, but disconnected until ICE returns", "a WHIP session whose DTLS never connects after the 201 is closed when the establishment timeout expires", "DTLS connecting stops the establishment timer, so a session that went live is not closed by it", "the establishment timer does not outlive the session: closeWhipSession and the OBS DELETE clear it", "a replaced session's grace timer never closes the session that replaced it", "ICE flapping before DTLS connects leaves no grace period or reconnecting flag behind once ICE is back"; regression guards that pass before and after: "ICE recovery does not undo a DTLS failure: the grace period still closes the session", "a replaced session's establishment timer never closes the session that replaced it"
issues.proof: The tests run the real WHIP router on a real HTTP server with fake mediasoup transports (the harness of TASK-036; the fake's close() now also drops its icestatechange listeners, as mediasoup delivers no events after close) and node:test mock timers for setTimeout. With the unchanged lib files, 10 of the 29 tests in the file failed: after transport.emit('icestatechange', 'disconnected') on a live session nothing happened (room.whipConnected stayed true, 'true !== false'; whipReconnecting stayed false, no grace timer, no host metrics), and after the grace timeout the transport was still open ('the transport is closed': false !== true), so a transport whose ICE consent expired without a DTLS close_notify stayed 'connected' forever; ICE recovery tests failed on the same first assertion; after a 201 with no DTLS there was no timer (room.whipEstablishTimer undefined, 'the timer runs once the 201 is out') and the session, resource and transport stayed forever; a replaced session's ICE grace period was never started, so the replacement test could not even set it up. After the fix: beginGracePeriod(reason) is the former DTLS-failed branch extracted, guarded by isCurrentSession() (generation and transport), now also started by 'icestatechange' 'disconnected'; on 'connected'/'completed' endGracePeriod() clears the grace timer, resets whipReconnecting, restores whipConnected=true if the session had gone live and emits host metrics, unless DTLS is failed/closed (that cannot recover; the grace timer still closes it, which a guard test pins). A session that finished its producers while ICE was already down is committed but left disconnected (whipConnected = iceState !== 'disconnected'). startEstablishTimer() runs when the 201 is about to be sent: room.whipEstablishTimer, WHIP_GRACE_TIMEOUT_MS (Q-005 default: no dedicated config key exists, so none was added), unref'd; DTLS 'connected' clears it, closeWhipSession clears it (also the fallback closer in lib/roomLifecycle.js), and on expiry teardownGeneration('ICE/DTLS establishment timed out') runs only if the generation is still current and DTLS never connected: relay stopped, closeWhipSession (producers, transport, resource), fallbackAvailable false, host told. Superseded-generation timers: closeWhipSession clears both timers and both callbacks check isCurrentSession(); the two replacement tests show a replacement session that went live survives ticks past both deadlines. Not tested directly: an icestatechange delivered by a superseded transport (VAL-050 last sentence): mediasoup 3.27.1 delivers no events for a closed transport, as noted for DTLS in TASK-036, so the isCurrentSession() guard in the handler is a safeguard. node --test tests/whipRoutes.test.js 29/29; tests/config.test.js 16/16; npm test 1263/1263; lint and typecheck pass.

issues.title: Raw H.264 SPS/PPS captured from one OBS session persist into later WHIP sessions and into a stale capture's writes
issues.test: tests/whipRoutes.test.js: "closeWhipSession clears the SPS/PPS and sprop a session captured", "a new WHIP session whose offer carries sprop starts its fallback relay without the previous session's SPS/PPS", "a sprop stream capture whose producer was replaced writes no SPS/PPS to the room and stops"
