issues.title: Session deletion does not verify the host bearer token
issues.test: tests/whipRoutes.test.js: "WHIP DELETE with no Authorization header / an empty bearer token / a wrong bearer token / a bearer token of the right length that is wrong / the host token without the Bearer scheme / the host token under another scheme gets 403 and leaves the session, relay and registry alone", "WHIP DELETE with another room's host token gets 403 and leaves the session alone", "WHIP DELETE with the host token returns 200 { ok: true } and tears the session down, once", "WHIP DELETE answers 404 for an unknown or stale resource without asking for a token"
issues.proof: Before the fix (lib/whipRoutes.js unchanged, the nine new tests added): 8 of 41 failed. Every unauthorized DELETE (no header, empty bearer, wrong token, wrong token of the right length, token without the Bearer scheme, token under the Basic scheme, another room's host token) returned 200 instead of 403 and tore the live session down: transport closed, WHIP resource unregistered, fallback relay stopped. The ninth test (404 for an unknown or stale resource without a token) passed before and after, pinning that the 404 paths are unchanged. After the fix: a bearerTokenFromRequest(req) helper (the POST handler's exact extraction) is used by POST and DELETE; DELETE returns 403 { error: 'Invalid or missing authorization token' } with CORS headers after the resource and room.whipResourceId checks and before stopFallbackRelay/closeWhipSession, and the host token still gets 200 { ok: true } with the same teardown. node --test tests/whipRoutes.test.js 41/41 (exit 0). The harness's delete() helper now sends the host's bearer token by default (an existing test, 'the establishment timer does not outlive the session', deleted without one and only passed because DELETE was unauthenticated); callers pass their own headers for the refusal cases. OBS sends bearer_token on DELETE (configureObsStream sets it), so the supported client is unaffected.

issues.title: Public WHIP rate-limit map is never pruned and is populated before authentication
issues.test: tests/whipRoutes.test.js: 'a flood of distinct addresses never leaves the limiter holding more than its cap', 'expired entries are pruned after the window without their addresses returning', 'at the cap the limiter evicts an expired entry before a live one', 'at the cap with every entry live the limiter evicts the oldest, and a window reset makes an entry the newest', 'the limiter buckets IPv6 clients by their /64 and leaves other identities as they are', 'the public WHIP router drops the oldest tracked address at its cap and keeps limiting the others', 'the public WHIP router's own IP fallback buckets by the client behind TRUST_PROXY proxies, not by the proxy' (and, passing before and after, 'the public WHIP router's own IP fallback uses the connecting address when no proxy is trusted')
issues.proof: The map was private to createWhipRouter, so the unbounded growth could only be pinned through an extracted limiter: on the unchanged lib/whipRoutes.js the six limiter unit tests failed with "createClientRateLimiter is not a function" (the factory did not exist; there was no cap, no sweep and no IPv6 bucketing to test). Two router-level tests failed on the unchanged code for the issue's own reasons: with a cap of two tracked addresses the dropped address was still limited ('the dropped address counts afresh: the map holds at most two addresses', 429 !== 404, because the old map never evicts), and with TRUST_X_FORWARDED_HEADERS on and TRUST_PROXY 2 a second client behind the same proxies got 429 ('a second client behind the same proxies shared the first one's bucket', 429 !== 404, because the default getClientIp was the raw socket address). 8 of 41 tests in tests/whipRoutes.test.js failed before the fix, none after. After the fix: createClientRateLimiter keeps at most MAX_TRACKED_RATE_LIMIT_CLIENTS (10000) entries, sweeps expired entries at most once per window whoever calls (so addresses that never return are dropped), evicts the oldest entry at the cap (an expired one whenever there is one), deletes and re-inserts a key whose window reset so insertion order follows window end, and buckets IPv6 clients by /64 (IPv4-mapped addresses count as their IPv4 address). The router's default getClientIp is now proxy-aware like the WHEP and socket fallbacks (TRUST_PROXY hop count, CF-Connecting-IP only under TRUST_CLOUDFLARE_CONNECTING_IP). VAL-055: server.js already mounts the public router with getClientIp: getRequestClientIp (server.js, in the PUBLIC_WHIP_ENABLED block after createWhipRouter(result.router, ...) with publicEndpoint: true), which resolves the trusted client through lib/requestIdentity.js, so no server.js change was needed. The pre-auth check, the 429 after PUBLIC_WHIP_RATE_LIMIT_MAX attempts, the config defaults and the non-public router are unchanged; the existing 'public WHIP enforces per-IP and global pending-start limits' test passes untouched. node --test tests/whipRoutes.test.js 41/41, tests/expiringTracker.test.js 1/1, npm test 1294/1294, lint and typecheck clean. Commit on lane/server (see TASK-040.md).

issues.title: Unbounded public WHIP rate limiting map leaks memory across unique IP addresses
issues.test: tests/whipRoutes.test.js: 'a flood of distinct addresses never leaves the limiter holding more than its cap', 'expired entries are pruned after the window without their addresses returning', 'the public WHIP router drops the oldest tracked address at its cap and keeps limiting the others'
issues.proof: Same change as C-f04e9d9c1539. On the unchanged code the two limiter tests failed with "createClientRateLimiter is not a function" (no bounded limiter existed) and the router test failed with 'the dropped address counts afresh: the map holds at most two addresses' (429 !== 404): the old map kept every address for the life of the process. After the fix a flood of 500 distinct /64s into a limiter capped at 50 never holds more than 50 entries, 10025 distinct addresses into the default limiter leave exactly 10000, and after the window one later attempt by any address sweeps the 20 expired entries out without their addresses returning. The three failure paths of the issue are the three tests above: a refused connect among several clients, a failing warm-up fetchMetrics, and a failing fetchMetrics in the sampling loop with the ack loops running. Each runs scripts/benchmark-runtime.js as a child process against a local http + socket.io fixture and asserts that the process exited by itself (not killed after 10 s), exit code 1, the failure message on stderr, zero sockets still connected on the fixture, that every socket that had connected ended with the server-side reason 'client namespace disconnect' (the script closed it, it was not dropped with the process), and for the mid-run case that acknowledgements had been flowing. The prompt's step 2 asks to close the sockets first and then await the loops; TASK-043 awaits the loops first on purpose, and that is right: checked with a scratch socket.io client, closing a socket while an acknowledgement is in flight calls its callback with 'socket has been disconnected', which would make the last in-flight acknowledgement of a successful run count as a failed one in the summary. issues.title: HTTP timeout does not cover smoke response-body reads
issues.test: tests/smokePackaged.test.js (new): 'the JSON read gives up at the timeout when the server sends headers and never ends the body', 'the text read gives up at the timeout when the server sends headers and never ends the body', 'a call that does not read the body returns at the headers and drops a body that never ends', 'no stage reads a response body outside the bounded fetchWithTimeout helper', plus 'requiring smoke-packaged.js exports its helpers and does not run the smoke' and guards for the helper's results, a non-JSON body, an unknown read mode, a server that never sends headers, an unreachable server and isReadyBody
issues.proof: Holds. fetchWithTimeout cleared its abort timer as soon as fetch() resolved (response headers), and every stage then called response.json() or response.text() outside any timeout, so a server that sends headers and never ends the body left waitReady, the static-shell, handshake, package-info and media-worker stages (and the readiness poll inside the worker replacement loop) pending forever and the cleanup after the stages never ran. The file also ran main() on require, so it could not be loaded by a test. Before the fix: the new test file failed 11 of 11 on the unchanged code (the helpers were not exported: 'smoke.fetchWithTimeout is not a function'; requiring the file ran main(), which printed 'Packaged executable not found' and set exit code 1). Because that failure is about the missing export and not about the stall, the stall itself was shown on the unchanged code with a script that extracts the real fetchWithTimeout from the file and reads the body the way the call sites did, against a local server that sends headers plus '{"status":' and never ends: with a 300 ms timeout the read was still pending when the check gave up at 5x the timeout (1525 ms). Fix: fetchWithTimeout(url, options, timeoutMs, read) takes read = 'json' | 'text' | 'none' (default 'none'; anything else throws a TypeError before the request), awaits response.json() / response.text() (or response.body?.cancel() for 'none') inside the try block, before clearTimeout, and returns { status, ok, body }. All call sites use it (waitReady, checkStaticShell, checkSocketHandshake, checkPackageInfo, checkMediaWorkerReplacement incl. its polling loop, checkGracefulShutdown's shutdown POST and /healthz probe, cleanup's shutdown POST); no stage touches a Response any more, the timeout values, stage order, log lines and failure messages are unchanged. main().catch(...) runs only under require.main === module and the helpers and stages are exported. With the fix: the JSON and text reads reject with AbortError after about 300 ms for a headers-only stall and a partial-body stall (asserted below 300 ms + 2 s), the 'none' read returns at the headers with body null, and driving the real stage functions against a fake packaged server on port 31847 (not committed) shows each stage rejecting at its own timeout (waitReady 2.5 s for one attempt, the others 5 s) with a stalled body and all passing against a healthy one.

issues.title: Packaged smoke can validate and shut down the wrong instance
issues.test: tests/smokePackaged.test.js (23 new tests): 'with a server already answering on the smoke port, the smoke exits before launching and sends it nothing' (runs the real script against a fake Nextra on 31847), 'a child that exits before readiness stops the stages at once, with its exit code', 'a spawn error stops the stages at once', 'a child exit during the static shell, handshake or package-info stage stops the run at once', 'a ready server that is not the launched executable or its descendant fails readiness before any stage', 'kill-media-worker is sent only while the PID serving the port is owned by the run', 'recovery adopts the replacement the original server starts as its child, while the launched child keeps running', 'a same-build copy that does not descend from the still-running launched child is not adopted', 'a code-0 exit of the child after kill-media-worker is accepted is a handover: recovery passes once the replacement is adopted', 'a late code-0 child exit after the replacement was adopted is still tolerated', 'without an adopted replacement the recovery stage fails at its deadline and reports the child exit', 'a non-zero or signalled child exit during recovery fails it at once', 'a replacement that does not run from the launched build is not adopted, and recovery fails', 'a simulated packaged run passes every stage in order, each destructive request right after an ownership check', 'the cleanup shutdown request goes only to a server the run owns', 'the pre-launch probe refuses a port where anything answers, and passes only a refused connection', plus unit tests for classifyChildExit, createChildExitMonitor, setPhase ordering, the process-list parsers (ppid), isDescendant, caxaApplicationDirectory and decideReplacementAdoption
issues.proof: Holds. The smoke used the fixed endpoint 127.0.0.1:31847 without checking who served it, only logged a child 'error' and never watched the child's exit. Before the fix the new tests failed 23 of 23 on the unchanged script (the 11 TASK-050 tests still passed). The decisive one runs node scripts/smoke-packaged.js with a launchable executable (a copy of node.exe under a unique temp path, which exits at once) while a fake ready Nextra holds port 31847. The unchanged smoke printed 'Starting packaged executable on port 31847...' and 'Initial packaged readiness passed.', ignored the child's immediate exit, and sent the foreign instance GET /readyz, GET /, GET /socket.io/, GET /api/package-info, GET /api/metrics and then POST /api/test/kill-media-worker. It was still polling that instance when the test killed it after 15 s. (With a non-executable file, Windows' spawn threw EFTYPE synchronously, so the first attempt did not reach the stages; the test uses a real executable for that reason.) The other 22 failed because the helpers did not exist ('smoke.createChildExitMonitor is not a function'). Fix, in scripts/smoke-packaged.js only. assertSmokePortFree probes /healthz before the baseline and the spawn: any answer throws 'Smoke port 31847 is occupied: ... answered HTTP <status>', a timeout or other error throws 'is not free', and only ECONNREFUSED goes on. classifyChildExit({ phase, code, signal, error }) follows the prompt's table. createChildExitMonitor(child) records { code, signal, phase, at }; setPhase moves forward only, over starting/stages/recovery/post-recovery/shutdown/cleanup; exited never rejects and also settles on a spawn failure; unexpected rejects only for an unexpected exit or any 'error', and carries an internal no-op catch. createRunContext holds the child, the monitor, ownedPids (seeded with child.pid), servingPid, ownership { caxaDirectory, portObservedUnowned } and an AbortSignal that the stages' fetches and sleeps use. An unexpected exit aborts that signal, so a failed stage leaves no polling behind. Every stage up to the media-worker replacement runs through raceUnexpected. After readiness, verifyLaunchedServer requires the /api/metrics process.pid to be the child or a descendant of it (listProcesses now returns ppid: Win32_Process ParentProcessId, ps -Ao pid=,ppid=,args=) and records its caxa extraction (nextra-<id>/<attempt>). checkMediaWorkerReplacement refuses kill-media-worker unless the metrics PID is owned, and enters 'recovery' right before the POST. It adopts a new PID under the Q-002 default (the port was never answered by an unowned process, and the PID runs from the same caxa extraction). One tightening on top: while the launched child is still running, the PID must also descend from it. Since TASK-058 the server starts the replacement as a child of the original process, so this holds for the real replacement, and it rejects another instance of the same build, which shares the extraction. Only after the child has exited (a handover) is ancestry not required. Any other answer fails the stage at once. The stage passes only with an adopted PID, readiness and a new worker PID, then enters 'post-recovery'; at the deadline it fails and names the recorded child exit. checkGracefulShutdown and cleanup's best-effort shutdown POST go only to an owned PID (cleanup also accepts a descendant of the child). After the fix: the smoke test file passes 34 of 34. The port test exits 1 in about 0.1 s with 'Smoke port 31847 is occupied' and no launch line, and the foreign instance received only GET /healthz. By hand (not committed), node scripts/smoke-packaged.js with a copied node.exe as the executable exited 1 after 4.3 s, most of it PowerShell process listings, with 'Packaged executable (PID 32504) exited unexpectedly in phase 'starting' (code 0, no signal).' instead of the 30 s readiness wait. Not run: the approval-gated packaged smoke on Windows and macOS (no packaged executable was built in this lane, and the prompt says to ask first). issues.title: Smoke cleanup can kill unrelated concurrent Nextra instances
issues.test: tests/smokePackaged.test.js: 'cleanup kills the tree of the executable the smoke launched and leaves a Nextra instance started during the run alone' (runs the real node scripts/smoke-packaged.js with the real process listing against a stand-in executable: a node copy under <tmp>/.../caxa/applications/nextra-<id>/0 that runs as caxa stub -> server), plus 'selectCleanupTargets picks the processes the run owns and their descendants, never another instance or a pre-existing process' and 'cleanup kills the launched child through its handle, the processes the run owns and their descendants, and nothing else'
issues.proof: Holds. Cleanup SIGKILLed every process whose command line matched the shared caxa nextra- pattern unless its PID was in the pre-launch baseline. Before the fix the script-level test failed on the unchanged script: the test started a decoy (node with a command line under <tmp>/.../caxa/applications/nextra-decoy/0) as soon as the smoke printed 'Starting packaged executable', i.e. after the baseline; the stand-in failed the package-info stage; the old cleanup then killed the stand-in stub and server and also the decoy: 'the smoke killed a Nextra instance it did not launch (PID 30408)'. The selectCleanupTargets and cleanup unit tests failed with 'smoke.selectCleanupTargets is not a function' and, for cleanup, with the child never killed through its handle (killSignals [] instead of ['SIGKILL']). Fix (scripts/smoke-packaged.js): cleanup(run) no longer matches patterns. selectCleanupTargets({ records, ownedPids, knownProcesses, baseline, exitedPids }) returns the owned PIDs (launched child, the server verified at readiness, an adopted replacement), every process seen in the run's tree before (PID -> command line, remembered at readiness, at adoption, before the shutdown request and in each shutdown/cleanup listing) and their current descendants by parent PID. Never the run's, and never walked through: a process with the same PID and command line as in the baseline (the baseline is now every process, PID -> command line, so it protects processes, not numbers), a known PID that now runs another command line (reused), and a process holding the launched child's PID after its exit was observed. A PID nobody holds still links its children (Windows keeps a dead parent's PID; on macOS a reparented process stays known through knownProcesses). The child is killed with child.kill('SIGKILL') while the monitor has no exit record; the other targets by PID; the runner's own PID is never a target. After the fix the decoy survives (isAlive true), the stand-in stub and server are dead, the smoke exits 1 for the failed stage and logs 'Killing the processes of this run: <stub PID> (...), <server PID> (...)'. Residual: a dead owned PID reused within the run by a process with an identical command line would still count as the run's; no creation-time check was added.

issues.title: Smoke process enumeration fails open, so leftover-process checks can pass without checking anything and CI can hang
issues.test: tests/smokePackaged.test.js: 'a process list that cannot be read before the launch stops the smoke before it launches anything' (real script, PATH emptied so neither powershell.exe nor ps can start), 'listProcesses throws when the process list cannot be read, instead of returning no processes', 'a process list that cannot be read in cleanup is a cleanup error, and the child is still killed through its handle', 'a simulated packaged run with real processes passes, logs the launched executable exit, and the smoke ends on its own'
issues.proof: Holds. listProcesses() returned [] on a spawn error, a non-zero status, empty stdout, ENOBUFS or unparsable JSON, and cleanup then reported nothing. Before the fix the script-level test failed on the unchanged script: with an unreadable process list the smoke launched anyway, failed verification ('The process list came back empty, so the ready server (PID 37792) cannot be tied to the launched executable'), skipped the cleanup shutdown, killed nothing, and then never exited because the still-running child kept the event loop alive: 'exit null SIGKILL after 20229 ms' (the test's 20 s limit), stub and server left running until the test removed them. The listProcesses unit test failed with 'Missing expected exception: win32', the cleanup one with 'no cleanup error'. Fix (scripts/smoke-packaged.js): listProcesses({ platform, spawnSyncImpl }) passes the spawnSync result through readProcessList, which throws 'Process enumeration failed: ...' on result.error (ENOENT, ENOBUFS), a non-zero status or a signal (with stderr), no output, a parse failure or zero records; maxBuffer is raised from 8 to 64 MiB. main() takes the baseline (takeProcessBaseline) before the spawn and throws 'Could not take the pre-launch process baseline, so the packaged executable was not launched. ...' without launching. Every later listing (readiness, recovery adoption, shutdown wait) now fails its stage instead of seeing nothing. In cleanup an enumeration failure is a cleanup error, and the child is still killed through its handle; if it does not exit within 5 s after SIGKILL that is a failure too and the handle is unref'd, so the smoke always ends. After the fix the script-level test exits 1 in about 0.1 s with nothing launched; the simulated run with real processes (stub -> server -> replacement child, real Win32_Process listings) passes and the smoke process ends on its own with code 0.

issues.title: Graceful-shutdown stage never asserts process exit, and cleanup silently force-kills survivors
issues.test: tests/smokePackaged.test.js: 'the requested exit of the launched executable passes the shutdown stage, in the shutdown phase set before the request', 'a non-zero or signalled exit of the launched executable in the shutdown phase fails the shutdown stage', 'a /healthz timeout is not a stop: the shutdown stage fails when the port never refuses connections', 'a process the run owns that is still alive at the shutdown deadline fails the shutdown stage', 'after a handover in recovery the shutdown stage waits only for the adopted replacement, and says its exit code is not observable', 'cleanup reports the processes that survived graceful shutdown as a failure, then kills them', 'cleanup reports a cloudflared the run started, or any new one, and never one that ran before', plus unit tests for evaluateShutdown and classifyShutdownProbeError
issues.proof: Holds. checkGracefulShutdown ignored the shutdown answer, counted any /healthz error including the 1 s abort as stopped, and never looked at the child's exit; cleanup force-killed survivors before its stale check. Before the fix, on the unchanged script: a child exiting with code 1 or by SIGTERM after the shutdown request, a /healthz that only times out, and a media worker of the run still alive after the exit all passed the stage ('the stage passed' where a failure was expected); the requested exit happened in phase 'stages' (actual 'stages', expected 'shutdown'), so the monitor classified it as unexpected; the handover case did not log the unobservable exit code; cleanup returned no error for survivors ('Missing expected rejection.') or for an owned cloudflared ('no cleanup error'). Fix (scripts/smoke-packaged.js): checkGracefulShutdown checks ownership, lists the run's tree, then setPhase('shutdown') and only then sends the POST; it is not raced against the monitor's unexpected promise. The pure evaluateShutdown({ childExit, survivingOwnedPids, postResult, deadlineExpired, portDown }) passes only a 2xx answer (or a connection reset or closed by the server, when the owned exit then followed), a child exit in 'shutdown' with code 0 and no signal (non-zero or a signal fails), or an exit already recorded in 'recovery'/'post-recovery' (neutral, logged as 'replacement exit code not observable'), a port that refuses connections, and no surviving owned process. waitForShutdown waits within one deadline (15 s) for the child's 'exit' (skipped after a recovery handover), a /healthz probe classified by classifyShutdownProbeError (ECONNREFUSED or ECONNRESET is down; an AbortError or anything else is not), and an empty owned tree; plain timers, no timer left behind. cleanup(run) sets 'cleanup' first; when the stage sent its request, any owned process still alive is recorded as 'Cleanup found processes that survived graceful shutdown: <pid> (<command>), ...' before the kill; the cloudflared check (any cloudflared not in the baseline, which includes the run's own) now runs on the listing before the kill, so killing cannot hide one. After the fix all these tests pass, and the simulated real-process run logs 'Graceful shutdown: launched executable exited (code 0, no signal) in phase 'shutdown'.' One existing test fixture was changed: 'a simulated packaged run passes every stage in order, each destructive request right after an ownership check' kept listing the launched processes after its fake server shut down; it passed only because the stage never checked for live processes, so its shutdown hook now also empties the process list (one line). PS1 (Q-001): scripts/smoke-packaged.ps1 is referenced by no workflow, package.json script or doc (both workflows run node scripts/smoke-packaged.js), so per the Q-001 default it was left unchanged and is recorded as retired. Not run: the approval-gated packaged smoke against a real Nextra.exe / Nextra-macos-arm64 (no package built in this lane).

issues.title: Pending sharing operations can continue after teardown
issues.test: tests/browser/host-start-teardown.spec.mjs: 'leaving the host page while the capture picker is open stops the late capture and creates no room'; tests/startOperationGuard.test.js (12 tests: 'a stopped start whose create-room ack arrives with no successor removes its room and releases its capture', 'stop, a new start, then the old late ack: no host-stopped, and the new room request waits for the old one', 'a newer start that supersedes a pending one without a teardown gets the same ordering and no host-stopped', 'a reload-preserving pagehide never lets the stale start send host-stopped', 'a reload-preserving teardown of a later start also blocks an earlier stale start's host-stopped', 'every stale exit releases exactly the resources that start acquired', 'a start torn down during OBS configuration stops OBS only when no successor owns it', 'a start torn down before its room request never holds up the next start', 'a current start settles its room step at the ack, so a later start does not wait for its transports', 'the settle wait is bounded; a stale ack after the bound is escalated and sends nothing', 'guard: ids, invalidation and the compensation fence', 'startOperationGuardFor keeps one guard per socket across view remounts')
issues.proof: Holds. handleStartSharing checked nothing after its awaits. The browser test stubs getDisplayMedia with a picker the test answers by hand, clicks Start Sharing, leaves #host while the picker is open (isSharing is false, so no leave prompt; the view unmounts and its teardown runs), then answers the picker. On the unchanged client (built to a scratch dir and served by the lane's server.js on a private port) it failed three ways: 'rooms created after teardown' Expected 0 Received 1, 'active rooms' Expected 0 Received 1, and 'late capture track states' Expected ['ended'] Received ['live']: the torn-down start installed the capture, created a room and published into it, and the room stayed active. Fix: src/lib/startOperationGuard.mjs holds one guard per socket (it survives a host-view remount). Each start begins an operation; cleanup, terminateHostSession, handleStopSharing, the unmount teardown and pagehide invalidate it (pagehide with reload recovery as 'reload-preserve'). After every await (capture, the room step, get-rtp-capabilities, getDevice, device.load, create-send-transport, each produce, setMaxSpatialLayer, configureObsStream) and in the catch, a stale start stops its own capture tracks, closes its own transport and producers, sets no state, opens no OBS control channel, and sends host-stopped for a room it created (or the stopObsStream fallback after configure) only when no other start owns the session (activeOperation empty) and neither its teardown nor the latest one was reload-preserve. The transport's connect/produce handlers refuse for a stale start, and the capture-track 'ended' handler ignores a stale start's track. Room requests (leave-room and create-room) wait until every earlier start's request has settled and its host-stopped is on the socket, bounded by 65 s (socketRequest's own worst case for those two requests); a stale start settles only after its compensation emit. One establishObsControlChannel(op) opens the channel only for the current start and drops a channel whose ready reports failure. The unit tests drive the same createStartAttempt/requestRoom code HostView uses, with a fake host socket and server (one room per host socket) and hand-settled promises: stop then late ack with no successor emits host-stopped and settles after it; stop, new Start, late ack emits no host-stopped, the successor's leave-room/create-room come after the old ack and its room stays active; reload-preserve emits none; every stale case releases exactly its own tracks, transport and producers. Mutating the guard (dropping the activeOperation check, dropping the settle wait, or compensating unconditionally) fails 4 to 6 of them. After the fix the browser test passes and so do all 12 media-flow scenarios (run as a port-shifted copy on the private server, copy deleted); npm run lint, npm run typecheck and npm test (512/512) pass.

issues.title: Retry Auto-Configure OBS can start OBS streaming without a live control channel, so teardown may leave OBS streaming at a dead room
issues.test: tests/browser/host-obs-control-channel.spec.mjs: 'Retry Auto-Configure OBS opens a control channel that pagehide stops OBS through' (failed before); 'a control channel that never opened does not stand in the way of the stopObsStream fallback' and 'a Retry that ends after Stop Sharing opens no control channel' (regression guards for the other two sentences of VAL-091; they passed before, see the proof)
issues.proof: Holds. The spec starts its own server.js with WHIP on (the shared Playwright server has it off, and the host view only configures OBS once the WHIP endpoint is ready) and stands in for OBS with page.routeWebSocket on ws://127.0.0.1:4455: a stateful obs-websocket v5 stub that answers the handshake and GetStreamStatus/StartStream/StopStream/SetStreamServiceSettings, and that can refuse connections like a closed OBS. Case (2) of the issue: OBS refuses everything for the start, so its configure and its control channel both fail (the alert shows and the Retry button appears); OBS is then brought up and Retry clicked, and the status reads 'OBS configured'. On the unchanged client (built to a scratch dir, served by the lane's server.js on claimed ports) the first test failed: 'open OBS connections after the retry' Expected 1 Received 0, i.e. the retry's configure connection had ended and no control channel was left, so a pagehide teardown had nothing to write the stop frame to. After the fix the same step sees exactly one open connection, and a dispatched pagehide puts StopStream on that very connection and opens no new one. Fix: the Retry handler takes the session's operation (startGuardRef.current.activeOperation) at click time; in the configure .then it does nothing when that operation is no longer current (Stop, a room that ended, unmount or pagehide), otherwise sets the status as before and calls establishObsControlChannel(retryOp), the same helper the start uses, whatever result.success says. The helper (TASK-063) already opens a channel only for a current operation and drops (and closes) a channel whose ready reports failure when the ref still points to it, so the ready-failure step needed no change. The second test (start against a refusing OBS, then Stop Sharing opens one fresh connection to OBS, the stopObsStream fallback, instead of handing the stop to the dead channel) and the third (Stop Sharing while the retry's SetStreamServiceSettings is held; the retry then runs to its end and leaves no open connection and opens none) passed on the unchanged client, since TASK-063 had already made the helper clear a failed channel and the retry opened none at all. Mutation check: removing the helper's isCurrent line, the retry's isCurrent line and the ref-clearing on ready failure makes the second test fail (Expected 3 Received 2) and the third fail (a live connection left, Expected length 0 Received 1). Checked with npm run lint, npm run typecheck and npm test (751/751); the spec was run with a private Playwright config (no web server) while holding the Playwright lock, 3 of 3 pass.

issues.title: resetAndRequestInit recovery fails permanently on one unavailable response and can hang with no timeout

issues.title: Non-quota append failures are terminal, never recovered, and re-reported for every incoming fragment

issues.title: Live synchronization overrides intentional pause
issues.test: tests/fmp4RelayPlayer.test.js: 'VAL-095: live sync leaves a viewer's pause alone, however long it lasts', 'VAL-095: a paused picture stays where the viewer stopped it, and play jumps to live', 'VAL-095: playing again clears the pause, so a later stall is resumed as before', 'VAL-095: a viewer's pause survives a rebuild: the rebuilt player does not start playing by itself', 'VAL-095: the player listens for the viewer's pause and play until stop()' (and the guards 'VAL-095: a paused element without a pause event is a stall or a refused start, and is resumed', 'VAL-095: the pause event that playback reaching its end raises is not a viewer's pause', 'VAL-095: a pause before stop() does not carry into the same player started again', which pass before and after, and are shown to bite by mutants)
issues.proof: On the unchanged player five of the eight VAL-095 tests failed for the issue's reasons. With the element paused and a 'pause' event fired, 20 live-sync ticks (0.5 s buffered ahead, more than START_BUFFER_SECONDS) called play() every time: 'live sync did not call play()' expected 0, actual 1 or more (the first tick resumed it). The paused picture was moved to the live edge by the same ticks. After a SourceBuffer failure the rebuilt player called play() at once although the viewer had paused. The player registered no 'pause' or 'play' listener at all (expected 1, actual 0). After the fix: the player keeps a userPaused flag, set by the element's 'pause' event and cleared by its 'play' event (listeners added in start(), removed in stop(); stop() also clears the flag). liveSync returns early while it is set, so it neither calls play() nor moves the paused playhead or changes the rate; maybeStartPlayback seeks to the cushion after a rebuild but only calls play() when not paused by the viewer. A play() refused by autoplay policy, or a stall, raises no 'pause' event, so it is still resumed by the next tick (guard test). The first tick after the viewer plays takes the playhead to the live edge (currentTime 1.5 -> 7.5 with 8 s buffered, test 2). A 'pause' raised by playback reaching the end (element.ended) is ignored. Mutants: dropping the ended guard fails the end-of-playback test; calling play() unconditionally in maybeStartPlayback fails the rebuild test; not clearing the flag in stop() fails the restart test; disabling the early return in liveSync fails four tests. lint and typecheck clean, npm test 1095/1095, vite build (into the scratchpad) exit 0.

issues.title: Reload-recovery reclaim treats every error, including transient timeouts, as a terminal room end
issues.test: tests/browser/host-reload-recovery.spec.mjs: 'a reclaim cut off twice by the connection is retried and the stored room is resumed' (failed before); 'a reclaim the server rejects as terminal ends the session at once and clears the record' and 'leaving the host page during the pause between reclaim attempts sends no further attempt' (guards, passed before). Unit tests: tests/hostRecovery.test.js (classifyReclaimFailure, reclaimRetryDelayMs, reclaimWithRetry, createCancellableWait)
issues.proof: Holds. The spec starts its own server.js on claimed ports, seeds the record {code, hostToken, ingestMode} in sessionStorage and puts a page.routeWebSocket proxy between the page's Socket.IO connection and the server that counts reclaim-host frames and, per frame, forwards it, cuts the connection right after the emit (what a lost link or a timeout looks like to the client) or answers it as a server that still holds the room. Case: the first two reclaim-host frames lose the connection, the third is answered. On the unchanged client (vite build into a scratch dir) the page spent socketRequest's own two attempts on the first two, threw, and terminateHostSession ended the session: 'Resume Sharing' never appeared (Expected visible, element(s) not found, after 20 s) and the record was cleared. After the fix the third attempt is made after the 0.5 s pause, 'Resume Sharing' shows, exactly 3 reclaim-host frames were sent, every one with reloadRecovery true, and the record is still in sessionStorage. Q-002 (error shapes): socketRequest tags a failure with a phase ('connect', 'ack-timeout', 'disconnect-after-emit' for timeouts, a socket that never connected and a lost connection; 'server' for an answer). lib/socket.js answers every reclaim-host rejection that means the room is gone (invalid parameters, reload recovery not enabled, room not found or token invalid) with createRoomState(RECLAIM_REJECTED, ...), which carries terminal: true; the handler's catch-all answer ('Internal error') and the client-side timeouts and disconnects carry no terminal field. classifyReclaimFailure(err) is therefore 'terminal' exactly when err.terminal === true (the rule onReconnect already uses) and 'transient' for everything else, unknown errors included; a unit test builds the errors through the real socketRequest and the real createRoomState to pin this. Retries: reclaimWithRetry makes at most 10 attempts inside a 25 s window (the server holds the room 30 s from the old page's disconnect and the reload has used some of it), each attempt a single socketRequest with at most 5 s to connect and 5 s for the ack (less near the end of the window, never under 1 s: socketRequest treats 0 as its 15 s default), pauses 0.5 s, 1 s, 2 s, then 4 s, no pause that would end past the window; it waits for a disconnected socket through socketRequest's own connect wait. A terminal failure returns at once with no retry (guard test: exactly 1 frame, error shown, record cleared). Cancellation: the effect's cleanup sets the cancel flag and clears the pause timer through createCancellableWait.cancel(), which also wakes the waiter; nothing is sent after it and the reply of a request in flight is ignored. The timer lives in the effect run's closure rather than a shared ref, so StrictMode's replayed effect cancels the first run and cannot touch the second (unit test 'StrictMode's replayed effect...'). Mutation check: with the cancel flag forced to false the browser test 'leaving the host page during the pause...' fails (3 frames when leaving, 5 after waiting). The retries also stop when the host starts a room of their own on the page (startGuard.activeOperation), see the .md. Checked with npm run lint, npm run typecheck and npm test (1028/1028); the new spec 4 of 4, and the 12 media-flow scenarios (port-shifted copy) and the two earlier host specs pass on the fixed build.

issues.title: When reclaiming a stored OBS room fails, stopObsIngest is a no-op because ingestModeRef is still 'browser'
issues.test: tests/browser/host-reload-recovery.spec.mjs: 'a stored OBS room that cannot be reclaimed stops OBS even though the page starts in browser mode' (failed before); the terminal-rejection test also asserts that a stored browser-mode room opens no OBS connection (passed before and after). Unit test: tests/hostRecovery.test.js 'shouldStopObsAfterFailedReclaim: a stored OBS room needs a stop, nothing else does'
issues.proof: Holds. The spec seeds {code, hostToken, ingestMode: 'obs'}, stands in for OBS with page.routeWebSocket on ws://127.0.0.1:4455 (an obs-websocket v5 stub that answers the handshake and records every request), and lets the real server reject the reclaim (the room does not exist: terminal). On the unchanged client the page ended the session ('Create new room' shown, record cleared) but OBS received nothing: 'requests OBS received' Expected "StopStream", Received [] after 10 s, because terminateHostSession's stopObsIngest returned at ingestModeRef.current !== 'obs' (a fresh page starts in 'browser' and only a successful reclaim sets 'obs'). After the fix OBS receives StopStream and the record is cleared. Fix: shouldStopObsAfterFailedReclaim(stored) is true when stored.ingestMode === 'obs'; on a final failure HostView calls terminateHostSession(reason, { ingestMode: 'obs' }), which hands the mode to stopObsIngest(modeOverride), which uses the override instead of ingestModeRef (the ref is not set, since the sync effect would overwrite it). With no control channel on a fresh page that goes to the existing stopObsStream({ password: obsPasswordRef.current }) fallback, and a channel, if one exists, is still used first; exactly one stop is sent, not one from the override and one from the ref. A stored browser-mode room does not stop OBS (the terminal test asserts zero OBS connections). Transient failures keep the record and OBS running until the window ends; then the OBS stop is sent together with terminateHostSession. Checked with npm run lint, npm run typecheck and npm test (1028/1028).

issues.title: Cancelling the screen picker on 'Resume Sharing' emits host-stopped and destroys the reclaimed room
issues.test: tests/browser/host-reload-recovery.spec.mjs: 'cancelling the capture picker on Resume Sharing keeps the reclaimed room, and the next Resume Sharing streams in it' (failed before); 'a resumed room whose media setup fails after the capture is still torn down' (guard, passed before and after). Unit tests: tests/hostRecovery.test.js 'shouldTeardownAfterStartFailure: a reclaimed room survives a failure before its capture is in use' and '... a reclaimed room in use, and every fresh room, are torn down'
issues.proof: Holds. The spec shares for real on its own server.js (claimed ports) with 'Allow recovery after reload' on, reloads, waits for the reclaim and 'Resume Sharing', then makes getDisplayMedia reject with DOMException NotAllowedError (a cancelled picker) and presses Resume Sharing; a page.routeWebSocket proxy forwards the Socket.IO traffic and records every event the page emits. On the unchanged client (vite build into a scratch dir): the page sent host-stopped (Expected not "host-stopped", Received ["host-stopped"]), the server held 0 rooms instead of 1, the recovery record was gone (null), and the button still read Resume Sharing because cleanup() cleared resumeRoomRef but not resumePending, so the second press created a different room (Expected "57PMCD", Received "ZJ2J94"). Output in dev-notes/results/TASK-070-before.txt. After the fix: no host-stopped, the server still holds the room, the record {code, ingestMode: 'browser'} is still stored, the preview's srcObject is null, the alert carries 'Screen sharing was cancelled. Press Resume Sharing to try again.', Resume Sharing is enabled, and the second press streams in the same room with no create-room sent. Fix: handleStartSharing tracks a phase (START_PHASES preflight, capture, room, media, obs in src/lib/hostRecovery.mjs). shouldTeardownAfterStartFailure({ resumed, phase }) is false only for a reclaimed room failing in preflight or capture; there the catch calls a local releaseCaptureOnly() (stops the tracks of this start's stream and of streamRef, clears the video srcObject and streamRef, touches no room ref), ends the start operation on the guard (invalidate 'start-failed', the attempt is over), sets status 'idle' and leaves resumeRoomRef, resumePending and the stored record alone. Every other case keeps the existing stopObsIngest, host-stopped and cleanup(): fresh rooms in every phase, and reclaimed rooms from the room step on (the guard test answers create-send-transport with a failure after a successful capture: host-stopped is sent, the server holds 0 rooms, the record is cleared, the button reads Start Sharing; it passed before and after). Stale starts still leave through abandonIfStale first, unchanged. Checked with npm run lint, npm run typecheck and npm test (1206/1206); the 7 host-reload-recovery tests, the 3 host-obs-control-channel tests and the 12 media-flow scenarios pass on the fixed build.

issues.title: Recovery permits changing ingest mode without replacing the room
issues.test: tests/browser/host-reload-recovery.spec.mjs: 'while a reclaimed browser room waits for Resume Sharing, its ingest mode cannot be switched to OBS' (failed before). Unit tests: tests/hostRecovery.test.js 'recoveredRoomIngestMode reads the mode a reclaimed room was created with' and 'isIngestModeMismatch: only a mode other than the waiting room's own is a mismatch'
issues.proof: Holds. After a real share with reload recovery, a reload and the reclaim, the spec checks the settings while Resume Sharing waits, then takes the toggle's disabled attribute away and clicks it (so whatever reaches handleIngestModeChange is tested too), then presses Resume Sharing. On the unchanged client the OBS toggle and the AV1 toggle were enabled, no hint was shown, the click switched the page to OBS mode (Expected not checked, Received checked), and Resume Sharing reused the recovered browser room without create-room and took the OBS path: no capture, and the browser-capture status 'Streaming (...)' never appeared. After the fix both toggles are disabled while resumePending is true, with the hint 'Locked while the recovered room waits for Resume Sharing: it keeps the ingest mode it was created with.', the forced click leaves the mode on browser (handleIngestModeChange returns when isIngestModeMismatch({ recoveredRoom: resumeRoomRef.current, ingestMode: mode })), and Resume Sharing streams a live capture in the same room with no create-room. handleStartSharing also refuses, before it begins a start operation and without touching the room, when the waiting room's mode differs from ingestMode: it puts the setting back to the room's mode and says so ('This recovered room streams from browser capture and keeps that mode, so the setting was switched back. Press Resume Sharing to continue.'); no browser test reaches that branch, since the toggle lock and the handler guard leave no way to the mismatch, so it is covered by the unit tests of isIngestModeMismatch and recoveredRoomIngestMode (the same helper now sets the mode in adoptReclaimedRoom). Q-003 was taken at its default (lock; no 'discard and create a new room' action). The server is never told another mode. Checked with npm run lint, npm run typecheck and npm test (1206/1206).

issues.title: Stopping or leaving while OBS auto-configuration is in flight lets configure finish after teardown and leaks a fresh OBS control channel
issues.test: tests/browser/host-obs-control-channel.spec.mjs: 'Stop Sharing while a Retry configures OBS stops OBS once that retry ends, not before it', 'Start Sharing again while the stopped session still configures OBS waits for that setup, whose stop lands first', 'Leave and Stop during OBS setup stops OBS once it ends, and a host view opened again configures OBS only after that stop' (all three failed before); 'a Retry that ends after Stop Sharing opens no control channel' (existing, changed: it pinned the immediate stop). Unit tests: tests/obsOperationQueue.test.js (14 tests: FIFO order, rejections, ownership claim and release, stale stop skipped while a newer live session owns OBS, stop for S before a later configure, teardown of S during configure then Start of S2 with the real start-operation guard)
issues.proof: Holds in part. TASK-063 had already removed the leaked channel and the state updates after teardown (abandonIfStale after the configure, establishObsControlChannel checks the session) and added an unqueued compensating stop for a stale start when no successor owned the session. What was left, shown with a stub obs-websocket (page.routeWebSocket on :4455, one global stream, a held SetStreamServiceSettings, an ordered request log) against a real server.js with WHIP on, on the unchanged client (output in dev-notes/results/TASK-071-before-e2e.txt): (1) Stop during a Retry: Stop's fallback stop went out at once, before the retry's StartStream, and nothing followed, so OBS kept streaming at the ended room (Expected false, Received true after 15 s); the changed existing test shows the same immediate stop (connections opened by Stop: Expected 3, Received 4). (2) Stop during the start's configure, then Start Sharing again at once: the new session configured OBS at the same time as the old setup (2 connections opened while the first setup was held, 'Connecting to OBS...' instead of a wait), the old setup then wrote its target over the new one, and the compensation was skipped because a successor owned the session, so OBS ended streaming to the old room (Expected .../C3AC5B, Received .../59NU5S). (3) Leave and Stop during setup, back to #host and Start again: the same, across the remount (Expected .../WFHTE8, Received .../9S8CC3). Fix: new src/lib/obsOperationQueue.mjs, one module-scope FIFO queue for the page with an ownership record (owner token, changed only inside a running queued operation). Every configureObsStream call (Start and Retry) and every non-unload stop run through it; the token is TASK-063's start-operation id. A configure claims OBS when its turn comes (skipped entirely if its session ended while it waited), and after configureObsStream a stale one sets no state and opens no channel; if the owner is still its session it stops OBS in the same operation (when auto-start was on or the configure succeeded, or when its teardown left the stop to it; never after a reload-preserving pagehide) and releases ownership. A teardown whose session's configure is queued or running sends no stop of its own (deferStopToConfigure; any open channel is closed); otherwise it queues the stop (channel.stopStream then close, or the stopObsStream fallback), which runs unless a newer live session owns OBS and then releases ownership. Only pagehide writes StopStream on the open channel at once, unqueued. A new configure waiting behind another operation shows 'Waiting for the previous OBS setup to finish...'. After the fix all 6 tests of the spec pass (18 of 18 with --repeat-each=3): one StopStream lands after the old setup's last request and before the new setup's first, none after the new stream starts, OBS ends streaming to the new room with its control channel the only open connection; the Retry case ends idle with exactly one stop after the retry's StartStream. Checked with npm run lint, npm run typecheck, npm test (1394/1394) and the whole browser suite (76 passed, 13 skipped as configured).

issues.title: Queue-overflow drops discard arbitrary fragments and resume mid-GOP; dropped fragments are still acked
issues.test: tests/fmp4RelayPlayer.test.js: 'VAL-107: after an overflow drop, fragments are discarded until one starts on a keyframe', 'VAL-107: interleaved drops never let a mid-GOP fragment in', 'VAL-107: a keyframe fragment that is itself dropped does not end the wait', 'VAL-107: a stall that keeps discarding fragments still ends in a fresh init request', 'VAL-107: the wait for a keyframe holds for the SourceBuffer built after the reset', 'VAL-108: relay-ack is sent for the fragments that were queued, not for dropped ones', 'VAL-108: relay-ack count equals the number of fragments queued through an overflow and a reset', 'VAL-108: an empty fragment is not queued and not acknowledged' (and the guards 'VAL-107: a keyframe ends the wait and the count of consecutive drops starts over', 'VAL-107: with no drop, fragments that do not start on a keyframe are queued as before', 'VAL-107: stop() ends the wait for a keyframe: the same player started again takes any fragment', 'VAL-108: a fragment seen twice is queued and acknowledged once', which pass on the unchanged code or are shown to bite by mutants)
issues.proof: On the unchanged player 8 of the 12 new tests failed for the issue's reasons. With a held SourceBuffer the queue filled to 600; fragment 601 was dropped, one slot freed, and the non-keyframe fragment 602 was queued at once (queueLength expected 599, actual 600), so interleaved drops resumed mid-GOP. relay-ack went out before the overflow check: after 700 fragments with a reset at the 15th drop, 615 acks were sent for 600 queued fragments (expected 600, actual 615); a dropped keyframe fragment was acked (601 acks, expected 600); an empty fragment was acked (expected none). Interleaved drops never reached the 15-drop reset (consecutiveDrops went back to 0 whenever a slot freed), so no fresh init was requested. After the fix: handleMediaChunk sets awaitingKeyframe when the queue is full and then queues nothing until a fragment with keyframeStart === true arrives while the queue has room; fragments discarded while waiting count toward MAX_CONSECUTIVE_DROPS, so a stall still ends in resetAndRequestInit (the 15th consecutive drop, whether queue-full or waiting); the count starts over when a fragment is queued. relay-ack is emitted after enqueue, so the count equals the accepted fragment count (600 of 700 in the overflow test). lastSequence dedupe is unchanged (a fragment seen twice is queued and acked once). The flag survives the overflow reset (the rebuilt SourceBuffer begins on a keyframe) and is cleared by stop(). Mutants: not clearing the flag in stop() fails the restart test; counting only queue-full drops fails the stall test and the after-reset test; acking before the checks fails four VAL-108 tests. lint and typecheck clean, npm test 1148/1148, tests/fmp4RelayPlayer.test.js 48/48 (12 new). issues.title: A timed-out mutation loses its already-captured rollback state
issues.test: tests/obsWebSocket.test.js: 'a mutation whose response times out after dispatch is still rolled back' (VAL-112; also 'a mutation that throws after dispatch is journaled once'; guards that passed before and after: 'a mutation OBS explicitly rejects is not journaled', 'a mutation that was never dispatched because its snapshot failed is not journaled')
issues.proof: Holds. createObsConfigurationTransaction.request captured the inverse with snapshotMutation, then awaited sendRequest and pushed the inverse onto rollbackSteps only after a successful answer; sendRequest rejects when the 5 s request deadline passes (obsWebSocket.js:86-89), and that rejection left request() before the push, so a SetVideoSettings (or any snapshotted mutation) that OBS applied late was never restored and rollback() returned [] as if nothing were open. The first test runs a real withObsConnection against a fake OBS socket (requestTimeoutMs 20) whose first SetVideoSettings is applied but never answered in time, then calls rollback(); on the unchanged code it failed at the final assertion: the requests OBS received held only the 1280x720 write, the expected restore to the snapshot (1920x1080) was missing. The second test (a sendRequest that throws on the first SetStreamServiceSettings) failed with '1 !== 2' writes. Fix: request() wraps the dispatch in try/catch; on a throw it pushes the captured inverse onto rollbackSteps and rethrows the same error. The success path is unchanged and there is one push per request (no double entry); a response with requestStatus.result false is still returned without journaling; a request whose snapshot call throws or fails never reaches the dispatch and is not journaled; rollback still uses the raw sendRequest. A timed-out StartStream or StopStream has no captured state (its inverse is the opposite request) and is left as before.

issues.title: Rollback of profile parameters that were unset writes an empty string instead of restoring the default
issues.test: tests/obsWebSocket.test.js: 'rolling back an unset profile parameter sends null so OBS deletes it' (VAL-113)
issues.proof: Holds. snapshotMutation built the SetProfileParameter inverse with parameterValue: String(previous.responseData?.parameterValue ?? ''), so a parameter OBS reports as unset (GetProfileParameter answers parameterValue null and the default in defaultParameterValue) was restored as an explicit empty string; obs-websocket v5 deletes the parameter when SetProfileParameter gets null. The new test runs the transaction over a fake OBS socket: AdvOut/Encoder answers null, Video/ColorRange answers 'Full'; both are changed and rolled back, and the SetProfileParameter payloads OBS receives are compared. On the unchanged code it failed with the Encoder restore carrying parameterValue '' where null was expected (the ColorRange restore, 'Full', was right). Fix: the snapshot uses normalizeProfileValue (null stays null, anything else becomes a string), and the payload goes out with parameterValue null (JSON null survives the wire). A set value still round-trips as a string (the existing rollback tests pass unchanged).

issues.title: Rollback restores configuration without waiting for stream shutdown
issues.test: tests/obsWebSocket.test.js: 'a rollback waits until OBS reports the stream stopped before it restores anything' (VAL-114), 'a rollback sends nothing after a stop that stays active, and names every step it skipped', 'a rollback whose stream state cannot be read treats the stream as active and sends nothing more', 'a StopStream OBS rejects is not a failure once the stream is confirmed stopped, and the rollback goes on', 'a StopStream OBS rejects while the stream stays active is reported with the stop failure', 'a start that timed out may have been applied, so the rollback stops it and checks before it restores', 'a setup whose stream cannot be confirmed stopped says its rollback is incomplete and restores nothing' (configureObsStream; guard that passed before and after: 'a stop that timed out is not journaled, so a rollback does not report a start OBS would refuse')
issues.proof: Holds. rollback() replayed the journal with one raw sendRequest per step, so the StopStream inverse of a forward StartStream (journaled last, so run first) was treated as finished the moment OBS answered, and SetVideoSettings, SetStreamServiceSettings and the profile restores were sent at once; unlike stopActiveStream it never polled GetStreamStatus. The tests drive createObsConfigurationTransaction with a scripted request function and an injected delay and clock, and compare request order. On the unchanged code the order test failed: after StopStream the next requests were SetVideoSettings, SetStreamServiceSettings, StartStream, with the three expected GetStreamStatus polls missing; the stuck-active test sent all three restores where only four status polls were expected; the unreadable-status test (a throwing request, a refused request, an answer without data, an answer without outputActive) did the same; and the configureObsStream test returned the plain 'streaming stopped immediately' message with no 'Rollback incomplete'. Fix: a shared waitForStreamInactive (also used by stopActiveStream, whose behaviour is unchanged: 250 ms x 10 polls, an unreadable status still counts as stopped there) polls after every StopStream inverse in rollback in fail-closed mode: only outputActive === false with outputReconnecting !== true confirms idle; a throwing, refused, empty or malformed status counts as still active. If idle is not confirmed within stopPollIntervalMs x stopPollAttempts (250 x 10 by default) rollback() resolves with 'StopStream: output still active after <ms>ms' or 'StopStream: stream state unknown' (preceded by the rejection comment when OBS refused the stop) and one 'skipped <requestType>' per remaining step, and sends nothing else; a StopStream OBS refuses while the polls show the output idle is not a failure and the rollback goes on. The bounds, the delay function and the clock are options of createObsConfigurationTransaction (configureObsStream passes them through a new optional transactionOptions). Also: a StartStream that throws after dispatch (timeout) is now journaled with its StopStream inverse, so the new gate covers a start OBS applied late; a timed-out StopStream is deliberately still not journaled (its inverse StartStream would be refused as already active and reported as a failed rollback).

issues.title: Rollback restarts the stream right after restoring video settings, skipping the settle delay the forward path uses to avoid an OBS crash
issues.test: tests/obsWebSocket.test.js: 'a rollback starts the stream again only after the video settle time has passed since the last video restore' (VAL-115), 'a video color restore counts for the settle time, and other restores and a missing video restore do not'
issues.proof: Holds. The forward path waits 1200 ms before StartStream because starting the encoder while the video output is being reinitialised can crash OBS in video_output_connect2; rollback sent the StartStream inverse (the inverse of the first journaled mutation, so the last step) directly after the SetVideoSettings and Video-category SetProfileParameter restores. The tests use an injected delay that moves a fake clock and a request log stamped with that clock. On the unchanged code the first failed with 'StartStream came 500ms after the video restore' (only a 500 ms restore in between, no wait), the second with an empty list of delays where [1200] was expected for a Video/ColorRange restore. Fix: rollback() remembers the clock time after the last video-affecting restore (SetVideoSettings, or SetProfileParameter with parameterCategory 'Video'; also when the restore's answer never came, since OBS may have applied it) and, before a StartStream inverse, awaits the rest of videoSettleMs (1200 by default, via the injected delay). With a 500 ms restore in between only the remaining 700 ms is waited; an Output-category restore or no video restore waits nothing. The forward delay(1200) now uses the same VIDEO_SETTLE_MS constant.

issues.title: Transaction deadline closes the connection before rollback
issues.test: tests/obsWebSocket.test.js: 'a setup that runs out of time rolls back over the open connection before it closes' (VAL-111), 'a rollback that fails at the deadline is reported next to the timeout', 'a rollback that never finishes cannot hold the setup past its hard cap', 'a rollback already under way when the deadline passes is not cut off', 'setup work still running when the deadline passes sends nothing while the rollback runs', 'a mutation still unanswered when the rollback begins is rolled back', 'a mutation whose snapshot is still being read when the rollback begins is never sent'
issues.proof: Holds. The transactionTimeout timer in withObsConnection called done() directly: it settled the connection, rejected every pending request, closed the socket and resolved the caller with the plain timeout message, so configureObsStream's finish (and with it transaction.rollback()) never ran over a live connection; a callback rejection that reached finish afterwards sent its restores into a settled connection. The tests run configureObsStream against a fake OBS socket (through a new optional connectionOptions seam that passes timeouts to withObsConnection) that logs every request and the close. On the unchanged code the VAL-111 test failed: log was GetStreamStatus, GetStreamServiceSettings, SetStreamServiceSettings:whip_custom, close, where the restore SetStreamServiceSettings:rtmp_custom was expected before close, and the result message was the bare 'OBS setup timed out after 50ms.' with no rollback status. The other six failed for the same reason (no restore before close, no rollback status in the message, a rollback already under way cut off at the deadline with the timeout message instead of its own result, and a dispatched but unanswered mutation not replayed by a rollback that begins before its answer or timeout). Fix: withObsConnection passes its callback a third argument { signal, onDeadline }; at the deadline, a callback that registered a handler gets the signal aborted and the handler called with the timeout result, and a hard cap (deadlineGraceMs, default 18.7 s = 10 x 250 ms stop gate + 1.2 s video settle + 3 request timeouts) closes the connection and settles with 'OBS setup timed out after Nms. Rollback incomplete: not finished <grace>ms later, so the connection was closed.' if the handler has not settled; without a handler the deadline settles at once as before; openObsControlChannel (Infinity deadline) is untouched. configureObsStream registers onDeadline(finish) so the deadline takes the same path as any other failure: rollback over the open connection, then done, with 'OBS settings were restored.' appended when the rollback was clean ('Rollback incomplete: ...' otherwise); a finish already under way is not restarted or cut off at the deadline (only the hard cap bounds it). Because a timed-out setup is stuck inside a request, createObsConfigurationTransaction now tracks mutations that were sent and not yet answered and a rollback replays them as it does a timed-out one (a StopStream is excluded, as for a timeout), and refuses to send a mutation whose snapshot read finished after the rollback began. The housekeeping stream test (releaseStaleEncoder) is sent through a channel that rejects once the deadline signal is aborted, so it cannot interleave with the rollback.

issues.title: openObsControlChannel().close() does nothing before the handshake completes, leaving the channel open for the page lifetime
issues.test: tests/obsWebSocket.test.js: 'closing the OBS control channel while it is still connecting closes the socket for good' (VAL-110), 'closing the OBS control channel while it authenticates closes the socket and never identifies', 'closing the OBS control channel right behind Identified never runs the channel setup'; guard: 'closing the OBS control channel twice, or after it opened, still settles ready once' (passed before and after)
issues.proof: Holds. close() could end the connection only through settleConnection, which the callback assigned after Identified (op 2); before that it only nulled sendRequest, so the socket stayed open, ready never resolved as a failure, and the handshake that completed later ran the callback, re-armed sendRequest and resolved ready with success. The tests drive a hand-fed fake socket (it records every frame written and the close) and call close() before the handshake. On the unchanged code: the VAL-110 test failed at 'close() has to end a socket that has not identified yet' (false !== true: the fake socket was not closed); the authentication test failed at ws.closed (false !== true) with the password hash still being computed; the right-behind-Identified test failed the same way (false !== true). After the fix all pass, and mutation checks show each guard matters: without the post-hash settled check the late identify frame is written to the closed socket (authentication test fails), without the settled check before the callback the channel opens and ready resolves with success (right-behind-Identified test fails). Fix: withObsConnection returns its promise with an abort(result) method that settles through done at any stage (closes the socket, rejects pending requests, clears timers; a no-op once settled). The WebSocket message handler ignores everything once the transaction has settled, does not send the identify frame if the transaction ended while the password hash was computed, and the callback is not run if the transaction settled between Identified and the callback's turn. openObsControlChannel().close() now calls connection.abort(): { success: true, 'OBS control channel closed.' } when the channel was open, { success: false, 'OBS control channel closed before it opened.' } otherwise, which is what ready then resolves with when it had not resolved yet (ready resolves exactly once). stopStream() resolves false after close; on an open channel it still writes one frame immediately (existing test unchanged and passing).

issues.title: Housekeeping stream cleanup is neither guaranteed nor verified
issues.test: tests/obsWebSocket.test.js: 'a test stream whose status request fails mid-run is stopped before the setup fails (VAL-116)', 'a test stream that cannot be confirmed stopped ends the setup before the video or encoder changes (VAL-116)', 'a deadline that passes while the test stream runs stops it before the rollback restores anything (VAL-116)', 'a test stream OBS refuses to start is still stopped and seen idle before the video changes (VAL-116)', 'a stop held for a stream started outside the transaction is rolled back only while it is held'; guards that passed before and after: 'a stop OBS refuses for a test stream that is already down is not a failure (VAL-116)', 'a setup that fails after a clean test stream does not stop the stream again in its rollback'; changed: 'setup work still running when the deadline passes sends nothing while the rollback runs'
issues.proof: Holds. releaseStaleEncoder sent StartStream, polled, then StopStream with no try/finally, ignored the StopStream answer, and after 40 status polls returned true whenever the stream had been seen running, active or not; configureObsStream then went on to SetVideoSettings and the encoder profile writes. Nothing journaled the raw test stream, so a rollback (also the deadline's, added by TASK-080) left it running. The tests drive configureObsStream against fake OBS sockets that log every request. On the unchanged code: a status poll that timed out after StartStream ended the setup with the log '..., StartStream, GetStreamStatus, SetStreamServiceSettings' and no StopStream ('the StartStream at 3 is not stopped'); with OBS refusing the stop, or accepting it while the output stayed up, the setup sent SetVideoSettings (and the encoder writes) after about 4 s of polling ('SetVideoSettings sent while the test stream may still run', true !== false); a deadline between the test stream's start and its first poll restored the service and closed with the stream still running (log missing 'StopStream', 'GetStreamStatus' before the restore); a StartStream OBS refused was followed by no stop at all. Fix: each run is wrapped in try/finally; the finally sends StopStream and polls fail-closed (only outputActive === false and not reconnecting counts as down; a request that fails ends the check unconfirmed), also after a failed request or a refused start, and the request error is rethrown after the cleanup. releaseStaleEncoder returns { released, stopped, message }, and configureObsStream ends the setup through finish when stopped is false, before any video or encoder change ('OBS could not confirm that the short test stream ... stopped (StopStream: output busy; output still active after 4000ms), so setup ended before changing the video or encoder settings.'). A new transaction.hold(step) journals a StopStream only while a test stream may be running and drops it once the stop is confirmed, so a rollback that begins meanwhile (the deadline, when housekeeping is refused) or after an unconfirmed stop stops the stream and passes the stop gate before restoring anything; after a clean reset nothing is journaled (guard test: one StopStream only). Mutation checks: removing the finally, ignoring stopped, removing the hold, releasing the hold after an unconfirmed stop, or skipping the stop after a refused start each fail at least one of the new tests. node --test tests/obsWebSocket.test.js tests/obsWebSocketWire.test.js 60/60, npm run lint, npm run typecheck and npm test (1059/1059) pass.

issues.title: Configuration broadcasts even when autoStart is false
issues.test: tests/obsWebSocket.test.js: 'without auto-start the encoder-reset test stream runs at the server's probe, never at the room's WHIP URL (section-49e0545c60d121dd3e784d86/Q-002)'; tests/whipRoutes.test.js: 'a WHIP probe is answered and connected like a start, but nothing reaches viewers, the relay or the host page (section-49e0545c60d121dd3e784d86/Q-002)'

With this change the test stream with autoStart false goes to the server's probe, which produces nothing from it, and OBS is pointed at the room only after the stream is confirmed stopped; no StartStream is sent while the stream service points at the room's WHIP URL. The client test failed on the unchanged code (StartStream target was the room's WHIP URL). See C-acd4cd6d33eb for the fix and checks.

issues.title: Encoder-file changes are excluded from configuration rollback
issues.test: tests/obsWebSocket.test.js: 'a failed auto-start writes the previous encoder settings file back before it says OBS was restored (VAL-118)', 'a setup that ends after the encoder settings file was written says when the file could not be put back (VAL-118)', 'a rollback that begins while the encoder settings file is being written does not claim it was restored (VAL-118)', and for the new transaction.registerUndo: 'registerUndo journals a step that is not an OBS request and undoes it in reverse order (VAL-118)', 'a registered undo that fails is named in the rollback failures, and the other steps still run (VAL-118)', 'a registered undo is dropped when it is released or the transaction commits, and cannot be added once it ended (VAL-118)', 'a registered undo still runs after the rollback could not confirm the stream stopped, while OBS requests are skipped (VAL-118)'; guard that passed before and after: 'a file write the server did not apply leaves nothing to put back (VAL-118)'
issues.proof: Holds. configureObsStream wrote the encoder settings file through writeEncoderSettings (a call to the Nextra server, not an OBS request) and journaled nothing for it, so any later failure (a refused auto-start, a request that timed out, the setup deadline) restored the OBS settings and left the file as written, and an AV1 setup or a timeout still ended with 'OBS settings were restored'. The tests drive configureObsStream against fake OBS sockets with a writeEncoderSettings double that records every call. On the unchanged code: with a refused auto-start the double was called once (1 !== 2, 'the file is written once and restored once') and the message read 'OBS configured, but auto-start failed: output busy OBS settings were restored. Disable AV1 mode and retry to use H.264.'; with the colour space write left unanswered the message was 'OBS request SetProfileParameter timed out after 50ms. OBS settings were restored. Disable AV1 mode and retry to use H.264.' for every kind of file answer; with the deadline passing during the write it was 'OBS setup timed out after 300ms. OBS settings were restored. Disable AV1 mode and retry to use H.264.'; the four unit tests failed with 'transaction.registerUndo is not a function' (output kept in the scratchpad as obs-TASK-083-before.txt). Fix: createObsConfigurationTransaction gets registerUndo(label, undo), which journals a step that is no OBS request (hold and registerUndo share one journal function); a rollback calls undo() in its place in the reverse order, a throw or rejection is the failure '<label>: <message>', and the undo also runs when the stop gate ended the rollback for the OBS requests (a file is not changed under a live output, so skipping it gains nothing). configureObsStream writes the file through the new writeEncoderSettingsFile: it registers a note before the write that fails the rollback while the write is under way (a rollback that begins then, i.e. the deadline, cannot know what the file will hold, and the write may land afterwards), releases it when the answer comes, and after a write the server applied registers the real undo: when the answer carries `previous` (a non-empty settings object) the undo writes it back through writeEncoderSettings and fails with 'encoder settings file: not restored (<reason or error>)' if the server does not apply it or the call fails; without `previous` it fails with 'encoder settings file: not restored (its previous contents are not known)'. A write the server did not apply, or that threw, registers nothing, as before. Since the failures list is what the AV1/timeout 'OBS settings were restored' sentence depends on, that sentence is now emitted only when the file was restored too; otherwise the message ends 'Rollback incomplete: encoder settings file: ...'. Mutation checks: dropping the in-flight note, ignoring a refused restore, and skipping undos after a failed stop gate each fail one of the new tests. node --test tests/obsWebSocket.test.js tests/obsWebSocketWire.test.js 68/68, npm run lint, npm run typecheck and npm test (1218/1218) pass. Not done: the server never reports `previous` (lib/obsProfile.js and the obs-encoder-settings handler are out of scope by the prompt's constraints), so against the real server every failure after a successful file write now ends with 'Rollback incomplete: encoder settings file: not restored (its previous contents are not known)' instead of a false claim of restoration; a real restore needs writeStreamEncoderSettings to return what the file held and the handler to pass it on as `previous`.

issues.test: tests/obsWebSocket.test.js: 'auto-start is not sent when OBS needs a restart for the new output mode, and the result says so (VAL-119)'; guard that passed before and after: 'with no restart needed, auto-start still starts the stream and the result says no restart is needed'

issues.title: WatchView reads window.localStorage at module load outside any try/catch

issues.proof: On the unchanged code the new source-level test failed (assert.doesNotMatch: WatchView must not touch window.localStorage directly; src/WatchView.jsx line 22 passed window.localStorage as an argument, so the property getter ran before isMediaDebugEnabled could guard it). WatchView cannot be imported under node:test (JSX), so the test reads the source, the same way tests/howToSecurityCopy.test.js does.
