issues.title: Status polling can continually abort slow metrics requests
issues.test: tests/metricsFetcher.test.js: 'poll ticks during a request slower than the poll interval do not cancel it', 'a load while one is in flight returns that same request and aborts nothing', 'a request that exceeds the timeout fails visibly and is aborted with a timeout reason', 'the timeout also covers a response whose body never arrives', 'a timeout settles the request even when the fetch ignores the abort signal', 'aborting for unmount cancels the request silently', 'an explicit retry replaces a stuck request silently and starts a fresh one', 'an abort the fetcher did not cause is reported, not swallowed', 'applyMetricsResult keeps the last metrics and shows the error when a refresh times out', 'StatusView polls through the single-flight fetcher and only aborts at unmount'
issues.proof: Holds. StatusView.fetchMetrics began with abortRef.current?.abort() and the poller called it every 5000 ms (and on becoming visible), so a metrics request slower than the interval was cancelled by the next tick; the AbortError was swallowed (if (err?.name === 'AbortError') return;), no timeout existed, and nothing was ever shown. The fetch logic lived inside the component, so it could not be run on its own: the new tests were written against a small extracted loader (src/lib/metricsFetcher.mjs, createMetricsFetcher({ fetchImpl, timeoutMs, timers })) and first run against a stand-in that carries the old StatusView logic behind that interface (abort the previous request on every call, swallow AbortError, no timeout). Of 20 tests 10 failed on it: the poll-tick test with 'the 5s tick must not abort the slow request: true !== false' (the 5 s tick aborted the in-flight request, which the old code did), the overlap test ('overlapping callers must share the in-flight promise'), and the timeout tests ('the request never settled': a request exceeding 15 s just hangs, with no error), plus the retry/abort-cause tests and the StatusView source guard (the view still held its own AbortController and abort-per-call). Fix: createMetricsFetcher returns the outstanding promise when load() is called again, gives each request its own AbortController and a 15 s timeout (DEFAULT_METRICS_TIMEOUT_MS, section-49e0545c60d121dd3e784d86/Q-004), and tracks why it aborted: a timeout settles as { status: 'error', message: 'Metrics request timed out.' } and surfaces through the existing 'Refresh failed' alert (or the Unavailable card before any metrics loaded) while the last metrics stay on screen; only an unmount abort (and a Retry replacing a stuck request) settles as 'aborted' and is ignored; any other abort is shown as an error. A race against the abort signal settles a request even if fetch ignores the signal, so a hung request cannot hold single-flight open. StatusView folds each result through applyMetricsResult in a useReducer; 401/403 still map to the Access restricted card; unmount calls fetcher.abort(). All 22 tests of the file pass after the fix. A real-browser run of the built page against server.js with a slow or never-answered /api/metrics confirmed it: an 8 s response rendered after a 5 s tick with one request and none cancelled; a request that hung after a first success showed 'Refresh failed: Metrics request timed out.' after 15 s with the metrics still on screen and the 5 s/10 s ticks joining it (2 requests total); with nothing ever answering the Unavailable card showed the timeout and Retry started a fresh request and recovered; a 403 still showed Access restricted.

issues.title: Superseded playback attempts keep mutating shared refs and the video element after awaits
issues.test: tests/browser/media-flow.spec.mjs: 'a relay start superseded by a socket reconnect leaves no stale playback, error or subscription' (chromium); tests/subscriptionLedger.test.js (VAL-156): "a stale attempt's late acknowledgement after a newer start sends no relay-consume-stop", 'a stale attempt that is still the latest claimant on the same socket sends exactly one stop', 'no stop after the socket reconnected under a new socket.id', 'no stop while the socket is disconnected, and no start either', 'a committed subscription is stopped once, by cleanupPlayback, and never again by its attempt', 'the claim is recorded in the same synchronous block as the start emit', 'a start acknowledgement times out once, and a late answer is ignored', 'canRelease and release act only on the latest claim of the same kind', 'WatchView and its session controller send relay starts and stops only through the ledger'; tests/playbackAttempt.test.js: stale detection, identifiable superseded error, own-resource disposal, current-attempt pass-through, and four recovery-guard tests (drop, coalesced follow-up with the chain intent, clearFollowUp and a failing recovery, re-entrant trigger)
issues.proof: Browser repro (the issue's socket-reconnect trigger): a tunnel-origin viewer clicks Watch; the test holds back the viewer's live media-init frames, so the relay-first attempt waits in its 7 s live media-init wait; the test then closes the viewer's WebSocket and socket.io-client reconnects under a new socket.id, so onReconnect runs cleanupPlayback and rejoins. On the unchanged code (vite build of HEAD c7489d0, server.js on 3210 under the Playwright lock) the test failed at 'getByText(/WebRTC mode active|relay mode active/i) toHaveCount(0)': received 1. The trace shows that about 7 s after the reconnect the superseded attempt rejected with 'Relay stream is not ready yet', and the handleWatch call started before the reconnect ran cleanupPlayback and its WebRTC fallback ('Trying mediasoup fallback', 'Mediasoup fallback connected', status 'WebRTC mode active (lowest latency).') in the reconnected session, with no click. issues.title: Disconnect-during-creation check waits a fixed 25 ms, likely shorter than the scrypt hash it races
issues.test: tests/roomCreationConcurrency.test.js: 'pending room reservations bound capacity, duplicates, failure, disconnect, and replacement' (the disconnect part was rewritten; the capacity, duplicate, failure and replacement parts are unchanged)

In a scratch copy of dev 84c0dd9 with the post-prepare guard in the create-room handler of lib/socket.js removed ('if (!reservation.active || reservation.cancelled || socket.connected === false) {' replaced by 'if (false) {', so a room is wrongly committed for the disconnected host), the unchanged test still PASSED (pass 1, fail 0), with the real scrypt (about 42 ms here, 3 of 3 runs) and with crypto.scrypt delayed by 200 ms: the 25 ms sleep ended before the hash finished, so the room-count assertion ran before the code path it guards. issues.title: WHIP start race tests never check that the rejected request leaves the winner's claim or pending slot intact
issues.test: tests/whipRoutes.test.js: "WHIP starts turned away with 409 while another is allocating leave that start's claim on the room in place" and "public WHIP starts turned away with 409 or 503 leave the running start's claim and the pending-start slot in place" (new tests with their own helper responseOrStuck, placed after the SSRC public-slot test; the two original race tests are untouched)
issues.proof: The gap was missing assertions, not a production defect: lib/whipRoutes.js claims the room (room.whipStarting, room.whipGeneration) and takes a pending-start slot (ownsPublicReservation) only after the 409/503 checks, and releases only what the request owns, so the new tests pass on the current code (node --test tests/whipRoutes.test.js 43 of 43) and no todo case was needed. The two new tests gate createWebRtcTransport on promises, hold a first start inside the transport, and then, before releasing it, send further starts through a helper that returns the response or a 'still allocating' stand-in after 1 s (so a regression fails an assertion instead of hanging): same room, two more requests expect 409 and after each room.whipStarting is still true, room.whipGeneration is unchanged and the transport was entered once; public endpoint with PUBLIC_WHIP_MAX_PENDING_STARTS = 1, each request from its own IP (.1 to .7, so the per-IP limit of 10 is never reached): a 503 from another room, a 409 on the starting room, and a further 503 from another IP, with firstRoom.whipStarting true, its generation unchanged and enteredCount 1 after each. After the winner fails with 500 the room is free and the next start is admitted; after the second start completes, two overlapping starts on fresh IPs admit exactly one (the second is 503, enteredCount stays at 3), which shows the counter is neither positive nor negative. Mutation proof, each mutant applied to lib/whipRoutes.js and reverted with git checkout (the file is unchanged): (1) the 409 branch sets room.whipStarting = false, (2) a shared finally clears whipStarting of the requested room for a request that never claimed it, (3) releasePublicReservation without the ownsPublicReservation guard (a turned-away request gives back a slot it never took, counter still clamped at 0), (4) the same without the Math.max clamp (counter goes negative), (5) releasePublicReservation subtracting 2 (counter ends negative after the winner). The two original race tests ('parallel WHIP starts admit one owner and clear the synchronous claim after failure' and 'public WHIP enforces per-IP and global pending-start limits before media allocation') still PASS on every one of the five mutants; the new tests fail on all five: mutants 1 and 2 at the 'the running start still holds its claim' assertion (true expected, false actual) in both new tests; mutants 3 and 4 at the further 503 from another IP (503 expected, 'admitted and still allocating' actual) in the public test; mutant 5 only at the final overlap of two starts after the winner is done (the post-release check, whose pre-release checks all hold). Existing assertions (whipStarting false and whipTransport null after failure, the 429 check, config restored in finally) stay in the untouched originals; the new tests restore config in finally too. npm run lint and typecheck pass; npm test passes 1303 of 1303.

issues.test: tests/obsWebSocket.test.js (lane obs, 4eafb14): 'a setup that fails after the encoder-reset test stream ends with OBS not streaming, and its rollback starts no stream (VAL-141)', 'a setup that fails after it stopped a stream stuck retrying a dead room puts the previous service back after the test stream, never the probe or the room (VAL-141)', todo 'a setup that fails after it stopped a stream stuck retrying a dead room leaves OBS not streaming, and the rollback starts nothing' (todo: C-2e1af7e99156); status assertions added to 'configureObsStream restores the previous service after a later validation failure' and 'rejected AV1 encoder candidates roll back to the prior H.264 route'

(1) Stale stream: with OBS retrying a room that no longer exists (outputActive and outputReconnecting true) and a setup that fails after the probe test stream, today's rollback ends with OBS streaming. stopActiveStream sends its StopStream through the transaction, so the journal holds a StartStream for it, and the rollback sends it after the previous service is back: the todo test fails on the unchanged code with 'no AV1 encoder is available: the rollback sent StartStream after it restored the previous service' (obs.order ends ..., SetStreamServiceSettings (room), SetStreamServiceSettings (previous), StartStream; status ends outputActive true, outputReconnecting false), and the setup's own message says 'OBS settings were restored'. The code cannot change in this item (src/lib/obsWebSocket.js is out of bounds), so that assertion is a node:test todo naming C-2e1af7e99156 (the plan issue for the rollback of that StopStream; no plan item fixes the restart itself). A three-line prototype in a scratch copy (a stop of a stream that was only retrying goes over the raw channel, not the journal) makes the todo test pass for both failure points and leaves the other 74 tests passing; it was reverted. (2) Idle OBS, setup failing after the probe test stream (no AV1 encoder; or every encoder write refused after a video change, via the new scriptedObs reject map): these pass on today's code and pin the rollback: OBS ends idle, the log ends with the restore of the previous service, the only StartStream is the probe's, and the service writes are probe, room, previous. Mutations of src/lib/obsWebSocket.js, each reverted: (a) the test stream sent through the transaction instead of the housekeeping channel: the two new tests fail, with 7 existing ones (the rollback starts and stops the stream again, so the final state is idle and only the order assertions show it); (b) stopTestStream returning at once without a StopStream: both withStream AV1 tests fail on their new 'outputActive false' assertion (true !== false), with the new tests and 11 existing ones; (c) the room write journaled again after the probe: the two new tests fail, with 6 existing ones.
